diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.mdx b/src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.mdx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..13f3f0f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.mdx
@@ -0,0 +1,328 @@
+import { Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
+import * as Stories from './DataGrid.stories';
+
+<Meta of={Stories} />
+
+# DataGrid
+
+Rows of data in typed columns, drawn in the look of a [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs). The
+grid is the part of the library that knows about the data. It is built in steps: today it reads the
+columns, formats each value for its type and its locale, and draws the rows with a sticky heading.
+
+**It is not released yet.** The grid is built in steps, and it is not exported from the package until
+the last of them, so this page and its stories are not in the sidebar of the published docs. What is
+here is what the code does today: **the API grows until release**, and a prop, a state key or a label
+that is not on this page is not in the code. The stories import the grid from its own folder.
+
+```tsx
+import { DataGrid } from './data-grid';
+import type { DataGridColumn } from './data-grid';
+
+interface Order {
+  id: string;
+  customer: string;
+  date: string; // '2026-11-05'
+  total: number;
+}
+
+const columns: DataGridColumn<Order>[] = [
+  { field: 'id', caption: 'Order', rowHeader: true, width: 104 },
+  { field: 'customer', caption: 'Customer' },
+  { field: 'date', caption: 'Order date', dataType: 'date', width: 140 },
+  {
+    field: 'total',
+    caption: 'Total',
+    dataType: 'number',
+    format: { style: 'currency', currency: 'VND' },
+  },
+];
+
+<DataGrid data={orders} rowKey="id" columns={columns} caption="Orders" locale="vi-VN" />;
+```
+
+<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />
+
+## Table or DataGrid
+
+Use a `Table` when you write the cells yourself and the data is small, or when the table is mostly
+text. Use a `DataGrid` when the data is an array of rows and the table should be made from it: the
+columns say what each value is, and the grid shows it. The two look the same, because the grid draws
+its rows with the classes of a Table: the variants, the sizes, the hover and the chosen row are the
+Table's own.
+
+## Rows and keys
+
+`data` is the rows; the grid reads them and never changes them, so a changed row is a new object.
+`rowKey` says what a row is known by: the name of a property of the row, or a function of the row.
+The key is a string or a finite number, and each row needs its own. A row with no usable key is
+known by its place in the list, and two rows with the same key are both drawn, as separate rows
+that selection and focus will treat as one; both cases warn once in development. Keys are checked
+when `data` changes, and not at all in production.
+
+A `rowKey` function is read as the rows are prepared, which is when `data` changes. Give it one that
+depends on the row alone; a new function on every render does not make the grid prepare the rows
+again.
+
+## Columns
+
+`columns` is an array of objects, not a list of child elements, so that `field` and the functions
+of a column keep the type of the row. A column reads a property of the row (`field`), or computes
+its value (`id` and `value`):
+
+```tsx
+const columns: DataGridColumn<Order>[] = [
+  { field: 'total', dataType: 'number' },
+  { id: 'tax', caption: 'Tax', dataType: 'number', value: (order) => order.total / 5 },
+];
+```
+
+`field` takes only the names of properties of the row, as strings, and the `cell` and `format` of
+that column take `value` of that property's type. This is why the column is a union: a column with
+a `field` and a column with a `value` are different shapes, and the type of the field's column is
+made for each property. The union is by design, so a type error on a column can be long; read the
+last lines of it.
+
+A column that computes its value has no field to name it, so it needs an `id`. An `id` is also what
+the state of the grid will call a column. It is the field when there is no `id`.
+
+The type of a computed column is lost when you write it inline in an array of `DataGridColumn`.
+`dataGridColumn` keeps it:
+
+```tsx
+import { dataGridColumn } from './data-grid';
+
+const tax = dataGridColumn<Order>()({
+  id: 'tax',
+  caption: 'Tax',
+  value: (order) => order.total / 5, // V is number
+  cell: ({ value }) => value.toFixed(0), // value: number
+});
+```
+
+| Column field | Does                                                                                    |
+| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `caption`    | The title of the column; the id when left out                                           |
+| `dataType`   | `'string'` (default), `'number'`, `'date'`, `'datetime'` or `'boolean'`; see below      |
+| `format`     | Intl options for the type, or a function `(value, row) => string`                       |
+| `cell`       | A function of `{ row, rowKey, value, text, column, selected }` that returns the content |
+| `align`      | `'start'`, `'center'` or `'end'`; by the type when left out                             |
+| `width`      | A width in pixels. Without it the column is flexible                                    |
+| `minWidth`   | The least width of a flexible column in pixels; 60 when left out                        |
+| `rowHeader`  | Draws the column as the heading of its row (`th scope="row"`); the first one wins       |
+| `lookup`     | `{ items, valueField, displayField }`: the value is a key, and the text is the item's   |
+
+A column with no usable `field`, or with an `id` that an earlier column has, or with an `id` that
+starts with `flg:` (the grid's own columns will use it), is left out with a warning. A field that no
+row of the first twenty has warns once, which is how a misspelt field shows. `sortValue`,
+`allowSorting` and the other fields of the finished column come with the plans that use them, and
+are not on this page until then.
+
+### The type of a column
+
+| `dataType`   | Aligned to | Shown as                                                                  |
+| ------------ | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `'string'`   | the start  | The text, which is cut with an ellipsis when it is longer than its column |
+| `'number'`   | the end    | `Intl.NumberFormat` for the locale; `format` gives its options            |
+| `'date'`     | the start  | The calendar day, `11/05/2026` in `en-US` and `05/11/2026` in `vi-VN`     |
+| `'datetime'` | the start  | The date and the time, short, in `timeZone`                               |
+| `'boolean'`  | the centre | A check for `true`, nothing for `false`; both have their words, hidden    |
+
+A value the type does not accept (a string in a number column) is shown as nothing, and a warning
+says so once, without the value. A blank (`null`, `undefined`, `''`, `NaN`, an invalid date) is shown
+as nothing too: the cell is empty.
+
+A boolean's check is drawn for `true` and the cell holds the hidden word `labels.yes`; `false`
+draws nothing and holds `labels.no`. The words are the text of the cell, which is what a screen reader reads.
+
+### Dates and `timeZone`
+
+A `date` is a calendar day with no hour, as in `DatePicker`: a `Date`, which is read in UTC, or a
+`YYYY-MM-DD` string, and nothing else. It is shown as that day whatever the zone of the machine, so
+the server and the browser write the same text.
+
+A `datetime` is an instant: a `Date`, a number of milliseconds, or an ISO 8601 string **with an
+offset** (`2026-11-05T09:30:00+07:00` or `…Z`). A string with no offset is shown as nothing and
+warns, since JavaScript would read it in the zone of the machine, which is not the same on the server
+and in the browser. It is shown in the grid's `timeZone`, `'UTC'` when left out, for the same reason.
+Pass the zone of the person (from a cookie or a profile) to show their hours; an invalid zone is `'UTC'`
+with a warning.
+
+### `cell` and `format`
+
+`format` changes the text of a value; `cell` changes what is drawn. Use `format` when the content is
+still text (it is also what a sort and a search compare), and `cell` for a Badge, an Avatar or a
+link. `cell` is called with the row, its key, the raw `value`, the formatted `text` and an object that
+describes the `column`; `selected` is `false` until rows can be chosen. A blank value is not given
+to `format`: it is shown as nothing.
+
+```tsx
+{
+  field: 'status',
+  caption: 'Status',
+  cell: ({ value }) => <Badge variant={value === 'Delivered' ? 'success' : 'warning'}>{value}</Badge>,
+}
+```
+
+A `cell` is called as a function while its cell renders, and is not a component of its own: to use
+a hook, return the element of a component that does.
+
+### Lookup
+
+A column with a `lookup` holds a key and shows the text of the item the key points at:
+
+```tsx
+{
+  field: 'status',
+  caption: 'Status',
+  lookup: { items: statuses, valueField: 'id', displayField: 'name' },
+}
+```
+
+A value that no item has is shown as nothing, with no warning: an app may keep rows that point at an
+item that was removed. A `format` function wins over a lookup, and Intl options are ignored for one.
+A lookup column is aligned to the start.
+
+### A stable `columns`
+
+The grid prepares the columns when the array changes. A new array on every render, which is what an
+array written in the JSX is, prepares them every time and throws away what was remembered of each
+cell. After three renders in a row with a new array and the same columns, the grid warns. Write
+`columns` as a constant outside the component, or in `useMemo`.
+
+## In a Server Component
+
+A column holds functions (`cell`, `format`, `value`), and a function cannot be passed from a Server
+Component to a client one. Write the columns and render the grid in a small client component, and
+give it only the data, which is plain, from the page:
+
+```tsx
+'use client';
+
+import { DataGrid } from './data-grid';
+
+const columns = [/* … */];
+
+export function OrdersGrid({ orders }: { orders: Order[] }) {
+  return <DataGrid data={orders} rowKey="id" columns={columns} caption="Orders" />;
+}
+```
+
+The grid still renders its rows on the server, so the page has them before any script runs.
+
+## Row height: `density` and `variant`
+
+A row has a fixed height, whatever is in it, so that a long list can be laid out by arithmetic.
+Cells have no padding above or below, and centre their content. The height is set by the `density`
+and the `variant`:
+
+| `density`       | `lined` | `striped` | `minimal` |
+| --------------- | ------- | --------- | --------- |
+| `'compact'`     | 31      | 30        | 36        |
+| `'standard'`    | 41      | 40        | 52        |
+| `'comfortable'` | 49      | 48        | 60        |
+
+The numbers are pixels, for a row whose tallest content is an Avatar `sm` (24px). A `striped` grid
+has 2px between its rows, so its rows are that much further apart. `compact` uses the `sm` size of a
+Table, with its smaller text. `rowHeight` replaces the number of the table with one of your own: a
+finite number above 0, or it warns and the table's number is used. The grid writes the height as
+`--flg-data-grid-row-height` on its root, and a grid in a cell of another has its own.
+
+`striped` marks every second row of what is shown, from the first, and not every second child of the
+body: the stripes belong to the rows, which matters when a window of rows comes in a later plan.
+
+## Height and the sticky heading
+
+With a `height`, a number of pixels or any CSS length (`'60vh'`), the whole grid has that height:
+the caption above it, and the frame under the caption, which takes the rest and scrolls. The column
+headings stay at the top of the frame while the rows go under them, over a solid colour
+(`--flg-data-grid-pin-bg`) so that the text passing under them is not seen through. The grid measures
+its heading and gives the frame that much scroll padding, so that what the browser scrolls into
+view is not left under it.
+
+Without a `height` the grid is as tall as its rows, and the heading has nothing to stick to
+vertically. The measuring runs only with a `height`.
+
+<Canvas of={Stories.StickyHeader} />
+
+## Widths
+
+A column with a `width` is that wide. Columns without one are flexible: they share the room that is
+left in the frame equally, and none is narrower than its `minWidth`. When the columns need more room
+than the frame has, the frame scrolls sideways. When no column is flexible the table is as wide as
+the columns are, and does not spread over a wider frame.
+
+The frame is measured after the first render, and only when a column is flexible. Until then, and on
+the server, the stylesheet shares the room out, so the first paint is already right.
+
+<Canvas of={Stories.FlexibleColumns} />
+
+A text that is longer than its cell ends in an ellipsis and does not make its row taller; a screen
+reader still reads all of it. There is no tooltip for a cut text.
+
+## Caption and name
+
+`caption` is the title of the grid, drawn above it by the element `captionAs` (`'h3'` by default, the
+level of a `CardTitle`; `'h2'` to `'h6'`, or `'div'` for no heading), and it is the name of the
+grid. `description` goes under it and is the description of the grid. They are drawn with the classes
+of a Card header, and without either there is no space above the grid.
+
+The grid has the `grid` role, and its name is, in order, an `aria-labelledby` you pass, the caption, or an
+`aria-label` you pass. A grid with none of them warns once after it is mounted. `aria-describedby` is
+yours joined to the description's, not replaced by it.
+
+## Props
+
+| Prop           | Type                                        | Default      | Does                                               |
+| -------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
+| `data`         | `readonly TRow[]`                           |              | The rows                                           |
+| `rowKey`       | `keyof TRow` or `(row) => string \| number` |              | What a row is known by                             |
+| `columns`      | `readonly DataGridColumn<TRow>[]`           |              | The columns; a stable array                        |
+| `caption`      | `ReactNode`                                 |              | The title and the name                             |
+| `description`  | `ReactNode`                                 |              | What the grid is about                             |
+| `captionAs`    | `'h2'` to `'h6'` or `'div'`                 | `'h3'`       | The element of the caption                         |
+| `variant`      | `'lined' \| 'striped' \| 'minimal'`         | `'lined'`    | The look of a Table                                |
+| `density`      | `'compact' \| 'standard' \| 'comfortable'`  | `'standard'` | The height of a row                                |
+| `rowHeight`    | `number`                                    |              | The height of a row in pixels, over the table's    |
+| `locale`       | `string`                                    | `'en-US'`    | The language of numbers and dates (see below)      |
+| `timeZone`     | `string`                                    | `'UTC'`      | The zone a `datetime` is shown in                  |
+| `height`       | `number \| string`                          |              | The height of the grid; with it the heading sticks |
+| `rowClassName` | `(row) => string \| undefined`              |              | A class for the row of a row                       |
+| `labels`       | `Partial<DataGridLabels>`                   |              | The words the grid says                            |
+
+The default `locale` is `'en-US'` and not the language of the browser, so that the HTML from the
+server and the first render in the browser say the same. Pass the person's language. Anything that
+is not a `variant`, a `density` or a `captionAs` is the default.
+
+`className`, `style`, `id`, `hidden`, `dir`, `lang`, `data-*` and the event handlers go to the root
+element, which is a `div`; a `style` of yours is kept, with the grid's custom property and `height`
+added. `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` go to the `<table>`. There is no
+`children`, and no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`: the grid draws everything inside.
+
+`DataGridProps` is an object type, so an interface can extend it:
+`interface OrdersGridProps extends DataGridProps<Order> {}`.
+
+### The ref
+
+The `ref` is a handle, not the element. For now it has one member, `element`, the root `div`, which
+is `null` before the grid is mounted. The commands of the grid (focusing, scrolling to a row,
+reading its state) are added with the plans that make them, and are not on this page until then.
+
+### Labels
+
+`labels` is merged over the defaults: a key left out, or `undefined`, keeps its English word.
+
+| Key   | Default | Is                                   |
+| ----- | ------- | ------------------------------------ |
+| `yes` | `Yes`   | The hidden word of a boolean `true`  |
+| `no`  | `No`    | The hidden word of a boolean `false` |
+
+## Do and don't
+
+- Do give the grid a name: a `caption`, or an `aria-label`.
+- Do keep `columns` in a constant or `useMemo`.
+- Do pass `locale` (and `timeZone` for a `datetime`) that the server and the browser both know.
+- Do put the columns and the grid in a client component when the page is a Server Component.
+- Don't give two rows the same key.
+- Don't write a `datetime` without an offset, or a `date` that is not `YYYY-MM-DD`.
+- Don't count on a text being fully visible in a cell: a long one is cut. Give the column room, or
+  show the whole text in a `cell`.
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.tsx b/src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..e4bcbb2
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,224 @@
+'use client';
+
+import { clsx } from 'clsx';
+import { forwardRef, useEffect, useId, useImperativeHandle, useMemo, useRef } from 'react';
+import type { CSSProperties, ReactElement, Ref } from 'react';
+import { dataAttr } from '../../internal/data-attr';
+import { hasContent } from '../../internal/has-content';
+import { joinIds } from '../../internal/join-ids';
+import { useAnnounce } from '../../internal/use-announce';
+import { useRequireName } from '../../internal/use-require-name';
+import { devWarn } from '../../internal/warn';
+import { withDefaults } from '../../internal/with-defaults';
+import { useHeadHeight } from '../table/use-head-height';
+import { checkFields, resolveColumns } from './engine/columns';
+import { createPipeline } from './engine/pipeline';
+import { createTextCache } from './engine/values';
+import { GridContext } from './grid-context';
+import type { GridContextValue } from './grid-context';
+import { useColumnWidths } from './hooks/use-column-widths';
+import { useColumnsWarning } from './hooks/use-columns-warning';
+import { useRowKey } from './hooks/use-row-key';
+import { DEFAULT_LABELS } from './labels';
+import { Body } from './parts/Body';
+import { HeaderRow } from './parts/HeaderRow';
+import { Toolbar, resolveCaptionTag } from './parts/Toolbar';
+import { ROW_HEIGHT, resolveDensity, resolveVariant } from './row-heights';
+import { uniqueKeys } from './row-keys';
+import type { DataGridHandle, DataGridProps } from './types';
+
+const NO_SORT: readonly never[] = [];
+
+const isPositive = (value: unknown): value is number =>
+  typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0;
+
+function DataGridImpl<TRow>(
+  {
+    data,
+    rowKey,
+    columns,
+    caption,
+    description,
+    captionAs,
+    variant: variantProp,
+    density: densityProp,
+    rowHeight,
+    locale = 'en-US',
+    timeZone = 'UTC',
+    height,
+    rowClassName,
+    labels: labelsProp,
+    className,
+    style,
+    'aria-label': ariaLabel,
+    'aria-labelledby': ariaLabelledby,
+    'aria-describedby': ariaDescribedby,
+    ...rest
+  }: DataGridProps<TRow>,
+  ref: Ref<DataGridHandle>,
+) {
+  const variant = resolveVariant(variantProp);
+  const density = resolveDensity(densityProp);
+  const labels = useMemo(() => withDefaults(DEFAULT_LABELS, labelsProp), [labelsProp]);
+  const captionId = useId();
+  const descriptionId = useId();
+  const hasCaption = hasContent(caption);
+  const hasDescription = hasContent(description);
+
+  const rootRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
+  const frameRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
+  const tableRef = useRef<HTMLTableElement>(null);
+  // The ref is the handle, not the element (spec 6.1): what a caller does with the grid are
+  // commands. The element is read when asked, so the handle itself never changes.
+  useImperativeHandle(
+    ref,
+    () => ({
+      get element() {
+        return rootRef.current;
+      },
+    }),
+    [],
+  );
+
+  // The name. The caption is the name unless the caller points at another, whose id wins; an
+  // `aria-label` is passed as given, and the description joins the caller's own describedby.
+  const labelledBy = ariaLabelledby || (hasCaption ? captionId : undefined);
+  const describedBy = joinIds(ariaDescribedby, hasDescription && descriptionId);
+  useRequireName({ 'aria-label': ariaLabel, 'aria-labelledby': ariaLabelledby }, 'DataGrid', {
+    otherName: { description: 'pass caption', given: () => hasCaption, watch: hasCaption },
+  });
+
+  const rowHeightIsValid = rowHeight === undefined || isPositive(rowHeight);
+  useEffect(() => {
+    if (!rowHeightIsValid) {
+      devWarn(
+        '<DataGrid> rowHeight is not a finite number above 0; the height of the density and variant is used.',
+      );
+    }
+  }, [rowHeightIsValid]);
+  const dataRowHeight = isPositive(rowHeight) ? rowHeight : ROW_HEIGHT[density][variant];
+
+  useColumnsWarning(columns);
+  const resolved = useMemo(
+    () =>
+      resolveColumns(columns, {
+        locale,
+        timeZone,
+        yes: labels.yes,
+        no: labels.no,
+        // The grid's own `allowSorting` comes with sorting; until then it is the default.
+        allowSorting: true,
+      }),
+    [columns, locale, timeZone, labels.yes, labels.no],
+  );
+  useEffect(() => checkFields(resolved, data), [resolved, data]);
+
+  const getKey = useRowKey(rowKey, data);
+  const pipeline = useMemo(() => createPipeline<TRow>(), []);
+  const textCache = useMemo(() => createTextCache<TRow>(), []);
+  const result = pipeline.run({
+    data,
+    columns: resolved,
+    getKey,
+    sort: NO_SORT,
+    page: null,
+    remote: false,
+    totalCount: undefined,
+    locale,
+  });
+  const rows = result.visible;
+  const rowReactKeys = useMemo(() => uniqueKeys(rows.map((row) => row.key)), [rows]);
+
+  const context = useMemo<GridContextValue<TRow>>(
+    () => ({
+      columns: resolved,
+      labels,
+      variant,
+      rows,
+      rowReactKeys,
+      textOf: (row, column) => textCache.text(row, column),
+      rowClassName,
+    }),
+    [resolved, labels, variant, rows, rowReactKeys, textCache, rowClassName],
+  );
+
+  // Only a grid with a height scrolls its rows under a heading, so only then is the heading measured.
+  useHeadHeight(frameRef, tableRef, height !== undefined);
+  const widths = useColumnWidths(frameRef, resolved);
+  // With a flexible column the table is as wide as its frame, and at least as wide as its columns
+  // need, past which the frame scrolls; before the frame is measured, and where it cannot be, a
+  // flexible column has no width and the stylesheet shares the room out. Without one every column
+  // is as wide as it says, and so is the table: spread over a wider frame, the widths would be
+  // proportions and not the widths.
+  const leastWidth = resolved.reduce((sum, column) => sum + (column.width ?? column.minWidth), 0);
+  const hasFlexible = resolved.some((column) => column.width === undefined);
+
+  const { region } = useAnnounce();
+  const rootStyle = {
+    ...style,
+    ...(height === undefined ? null : { height }),
+    '--flg-data-grid-row-height': `${dataRowHeight}px`,
+  } as CSSProperties;
+
+  return (
+    <GridContext.Provider value={context as GridContextValue}>
+      <div
+        ref={rootRef}
+        className={clsx('flg-data-grid', className)}
+        style={rootStyle}
+        data-variant={variant}
+        data-density={density}
+        {...rest}
+      >
+        <Toolbar
+          caption={caption}
+          description={description}
+          captionAs={resolveCaptionTag(captionAs)}
+          captionId={captionId}
+          descriptionId={descriptionId}
+        />
+        <div className="flg-data-grid-main">
+          <div
+            ref={frameRef}
+            className="flg-table-frame flg-data-grid-frame"
+            data-variant={variant}
+            data-size={density === 'compact' ? 'sm' : 'md'}
+            data-sticky-header={dataAttr(true)}
+          >
+            <table
+              ref={tableRef}
+              className="flg-table flg-data-grid-table"
+              role="grid"
+              aria-label={ariaLabel}
+              aria-labelledby={labelledBy}
+              aria-describedby={describedBy}
+              style={{
+                minWidth: leastWidth,
+                width: hasFlexible || leastWidth === 0 ? undefined : leastWidth,
+              }}
+            >
+              <colgroup>
+                {resolved.map((column, index) => (
+                  <col key={column.id} style={{ width: widths ? widths[index] : column.width }} />
+                ))}
+              </colgroup>
+              <HeaderRow />
+              <Body />
+            </table>
+          </div>
+        </div>
+        {region}
+      </div>
+    </GridContext.Provider>
+  );
+}
+
+/**
+ * A data grid: rows of data in columns, in the look of a Table. It is a generic component, so
+ * `TRow` is read from `data`; the `forwardRef` is cast to say so (React 18.3 and 19 both). Its ref
+ * is a handle (`DataGridHandle`), not the element.
+ */
+export const DataGrid = forwardRef(DataGridImpl) as (<TRow>(
+  props: DataGridProps<TRow> & { ref?: Ref<DataGridHandle> },
+) => ReactElement) & { displayName?: string };
+DataGrid.displayName = 'DataGrid';
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/grid-context.ts b/src/components/data-grid/grid-context.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..b004559
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/grid-context.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@
+import { createContext, useContext } from 'react';
+import type { ResolvedColumn } from './engine/columns';
+import type { FlatRow } from './engine/flatten';
+import type { DataGridLabels } from './types';
+import type { TableVariant } from '../table/Table';
+
+/** What the parts of one grid share. Internal: nothing of it is exported. */
+export interface GridContextValue<TRow = unknown> {
+  columns: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[];
+  labels: DataGridLabels;
+  variant: TableVariant;
+  /** The rows to draw, in order: the page now, and later the window of a virtual list. */
+  rows: readonly FlatRow<TRow>[];
+  /** A unique React key for each of `rows`, in the same order. */
+  rowReactKeys: readonly string[];
+  /** The text of a cell, written once for a row and a column. */
+  textOf: (row: TRow, column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>) => string;
+  rowClassName: ((row: TRow) => string | undefined) | undefined;
+}
+
+export const GridContext = createContext<GridContextValue | null>(null);
+
+/**
+ * The context of the grid the part is in. The parts are internal and always inside a grid, so a
+ * missing context is a mistake of the library's own, not of a caller; it is the one place that throws.
+ */
+export function useGridContext<TRow>(): GridContextValue<TRow> {
+  const context = useContext(GridContext);
+  if (!context) throw new Error('A part of the DataGrid was used outside a DataGrid.');
+  return context as GridContextValue<TRow>;
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-column-widths.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-column-widths.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..6622f57
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-column-widths.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+import { useMemo, useState } from 'react';
+import type { RefObject } from 'react';
+import { useIsoLayoutEffect } from '../../../internal/use-iso-layout-effect';
+import { resolveWidths } from '../engine/layout';
+import type { WidthSpec } from '../engine/layout';
+
+/** The custom property of the frame that holds the width the columns share, for what spans them. */
+export const FRAME_WIDTH_PROPERTY = '--flg-data-grid-frame-width';
+
+// The room for the table: the frame without its scrollbar and its own padding (a `striped` frame
+// has 6px). `clientWidth` is the layout size, which a transform does not change.
+function roomOf(frame: HTMLElement): number {
+  const style = getComputedStyle(frame);
+  const padding =
+    (Number.parseFloat(style.paddingLeft) || 0) + (Number.parseFloat(style.paddingRight) || 0);
+  return Math.max(0, frame.clientWidth - padding);
+}
+
+/**
+ * The width in pixels of each column, once the frame has been measured; `undefined` until then and
+ * when every column has a width of its own. Only a grid with a flexible column watches its frame
+ * (Task 7 adds the grid that shows something across every column): with none, nothing is observed
+ * and the widths are the columns' own. The room is written to the frame as
+ * `--flg-data-grid-frame-width`, which the stylesheet declares itself so a grid in a cell of
+ * another never takes the outer one's, and taken off again when the watching stops.
+ */
+export function useColumnWidths(
+  frameRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>,
+  columns: readonly WidthSpec[],
+): number[] | undefined {
+  const flexible = columns.some((column) => column.width === undefined);
+  const [room, setRoom] = useState<number | undefined>(undefined);
+
+  useIsoLayoutEffect(() => {
+    const frame = frameRef.current;
+    if (!flexible || !frame) return undefined;
+    const measure = () => {
+      const width = roomOf(frame);
+      // Not measured (jsdom, a hidden grid): the columns keep what the stylesheet gives them.
+      if (width <= 0) return;
+      frame.style.setProperty(FRAME_WIDTH_PROPERTY, `${width}px`);
+      setRoom(width);
+    };
+    measure();
+    const observer =
+      typeof ResizeObserver === 'undefined' ? undefined : new ResizeObserver(measure);
+    observer?.observe(frame);
+    return () => {
+      observer?.disconnect();
+      frame.style.removeProperty(FRAME_WIDTH_PROPERTY);
+    };
+  }, [frameRef, flexible]);
+
+  return useMemo(
+    () => (flexible && room !== undefined ? resolveWidths(columns, room) : undefined),
+    [flexible, room, columns],
+  );
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-columns-warning.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-columns-warning.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..824c72b
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-columns-warning.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,35 @@
+import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
+import { devWarn, isProduction } from '../../../internal/warn';
+import type { DataGridColumn } from '../types';
+
+const COMMITS = 3;
+
+const idOf = (column: DataGridColumn<never>): string => {
+  const { id, field } = column as { id?: unknown; field?: unknown };
+  return typeof id === 'string' ? id : typeof field === 'string' ? field : '';
+};
+
+/**
+ * Development only: warns when `columns` is a new array on three commits in a row with the same
+ * columns in it, which is what an array written in the JSX is. Every render then resolves every
+ * column again and throws away what was remembered of the rows. It counts commits, in an effect,
+ * and not renders, so StrictMode's second render does not count; a commit that keeps the array
+ * starts the count again.
+ */
+export function useColumnsWarning<TRow>(columns: readonly DataGridColumn<TRow>[]): void {
+  const last = useRef<{ columns: readonly unknown[]; ids: string } | null>(null);
+  const streak = useRef(0);
+  useEffect(() => {
+    if (isProduction()) return;
+    const ids = columns.map(idOf).join('\u0001');
+    const before = last.current;
+    streak.current =
+      before && before.columns !== columns && before.ids === ids ? streak.current + 1 : 0;
+    last.current = { columns, ids };
+    if (streak.current === COMMITS) {
+      devWarn(
+        '<DataGrid> columns is a new array on every render; pass a stable one (a module constant or useMemo).',
+      );
+    }
+  });
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-row-key.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-row-key.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..9448736
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-row-key.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,41 @@
+import { useEffect, useMemo, useRef } from 'react';
+import { useWriteOnCommit } from '../../../internal/use-write-on-commit';
+import { checkKeys, readRowKey, usableKey } from '../row-keys';
+import type { RowKey } from '../row-keys';
+import type { DataGridKey } from '../types';
+
+/**
+ * The function the pipeline reads a row's key with. Its identity is an input of the flatten step,
+ * which runs again when it changes, so it must not change when the caller writes `rowKey` as a
+ * function in the JSX, which is a new function on every render: the latest one is read through a
+ * ref, written at each commit. A property name is a value and can be a dependency itself. A row
+ * with no usable key is known by its place in the list; the warning is `checkKeys`', after the
+ * commit and only in development.
+ */
+export function useRowKey<TRow>(
+  rowKey: RowKey<TRow>,
+  data: readonly TRow[],
+): (row: TRow, index: number) => DataGridKey {
+  const field = typeof rowKey === 'string' ? rowKey : undefined;
+  const given = typeof rowKey === 'function' ? rowKey : null;
+  const latest = useRef<((row: TRow) => DataGridKey) | null>(null);
+  // Set while rendering only the first time a function is seen, which is how a ref is started; after
+  // that a commit writes it. A render that is thrown away never leaves its function behind.
+  if (latest.current === null) latest.current = given;
+  useWriteOnCommit(() => {
+    latest.current = given;
+  });
+
+  useEffect(() => {
+    const key = field ?? latest.current;
+    if (key) checkKeys(data, key);
+  }, [data, field]);
+
+  return useMemo(
+    () => (row, index) => {
+      const key = field ?? latest.current;
+      return (key ? usableKey(readRowKey(key, row)) : undefined) ?? index;
+    },
+    [field],
+  );
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,21 @@
+import { useGridContext } from '../grid-context';
+import { DataRow } from './DataRow';
+
+/**
+ * The rows. A stripe is on the even rows of what is drawn and not on the even children of the
+ * `<tbody>`, so it stays with its row when rows come and go at the top of a window.
+ */
+export function Body() {
+  const { rows, rowReactKeys, variant } = useGridContext();
+  return (
+    <tbody className="flg-table-body">
+      {rows.map((flat, index) => (
+        <DataRow
+          key={rowReactKeys[index]}
+          flat={flat}
+          stripe={variant === 'striped' && index % 2 === 0}
+        />
+      ))}
+    </tbody>
+  );
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/parts/Cell.tsx b/src/components/data-grid/parts/Cell.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..739db3e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/parts/Cell.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,55 @@
+import { CheckIcon } from '../../../internal/icons';
+import type { ResolvedColumn } from '../engine/columns';
+import type { FlatRow } from '../engine/flatten';
+import { useGridContext } from '../grid-context';
+
+interface CellProps<TRow> {
+  column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>;
+  flat: FlatRow<TRow>;
+}
+
+/**
+ * A cell of a data row: a `<td>`, or the `<th scope="row">` of the row header column. The `cell` of
+ * the column replaces what is in it; otherwise it is the text of the column, which is nothing for a
+ * blank value. A boolean is a check for `true` and no mark for `false`; the words are in the cell
+ * for a screen reader, and are what a search and an export read.
+ */
+export function Cell<TRow>({ column, flat }: CellProps<TRow>) {
+  const { textOf } = useGridContext<TRow>();
+  const text = textOf(flat.row, column);
+  const value = column.value(flat.row);
+  let content;
+  if (column.cell) {
+    content = column.cell({
+      row: flat.row,
+      rowKey: flat.key,
+      value,
+      text,
+      column: column.info,
+      // Selection comes with its own plan.
+      selected: false,
+    });
+  } else if (column.dataType === 'boolean' && typeof value === 'boolean') {
+    content = (
+      <>
+        {value && (
+          <span className="flg-data-grid-check">
+            <CheckIcon width={16} height={16} />
+          </span>
+        )}
+        <span className="flg-visually-hidden">{text}</span>
+      </>
+    );
+  } else {
+    content = text === '' ? null : text;
+  }
+  return column.rowHeader ? (
+    <th scope="row" className="flg-table-head flg-data-grid-cell" data-align={column.align}>
+      {content}
+    </th>
+  ) : (
+    <td className="flg-table-cell flg-data-grid-cell" data-align={column.align}>
+      {content}
+    </td>
+  );
+}

+import { clsx } from 'clsx';
+import { dataAttr } from '../../../internal/data-attr';
+import type { FlatRow } from '../engine/flatten';
+import { useGridContext } from '../grid-context';
+import { Cell } from './Cell';
+
+interface DataRowProps<TRow> {
+  flat: FlatRow<TRow>;
+  /** Whether this row has the stripe of a `striped` grid. */
+  stripe: boolean;
+}
+
+export function DataRow<TRow>({ flat, stripe }: DataRowProps<TRow>) {
+  const { columns, rowClassName } = useGridContext<TRow>();
+  return (
+    <tr
+      className={clsx('flg-table-row', 'flg-data-grid-row', rowClassName?.(flat.row))}
+      data-stripe={dataAttr(stripe)}
+    >
+      {columns.map((column) => (
+        <Cell key={column.id} column={column} flat={flat} />
+      ))}
+    </tr>
+  );
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
+import { hasContent } from '../../../internal/has-content';
+
+export type CaptionTag = 'h2' | 'h3' | 'h4' | 'h5' | 'h6' | 'div';
+
+const CAPTION_TAGS: readonly CaptionTag[] = ['h2', 'h3', 'h4', 'h5', 'h6', 'div'];
+
+// A value outside the union is `h3`, as a CardTitle; the list narrows it without a cast.
+export const resolveCaptionTag = (value: unknown): CaptionTag =>
+  CAPTION_TAGS.find((tag) => tag === value) ?? 'h3';
+
+export interface ToolbarProps {
+  caption: ReactNode;
+  description: ReactNode;
+  captionAs: CaptionTag;
+  captionId: string;
+  descriptionId: string;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The row above the grid. Only the caption block is in it for now, drawn with the classes of a
+ * Card header (spec 4.3): the caption names the grid and the description describes it. Without
+ * either there is no toolbar at all.
+ */
+export function Toolbar({
+  caption,
+  description,
+  captionAs: Title,
+  captionId,
+  descriptionId,
+}: ToolbarProps) {
+  const hasCaption = hasContent(caption);
+  const hasDescription = hasContent(description);
+  if (!hasCaption && !hasDescription) return null;
+  return (
+    <div className="flg-data-grid-toolbar">
+      <div className="flg-card-header flg-data-grid-caption">
+        {hasCaption && (
+          <Title id={captionId} className="flg-card-title">
+            {caption}
+          </Title>
+        )}
+        {hasDescription && (
+          <div id={descriptionId} className="flg-card-description">
+            {description}
+          </div>
+        )}
+      </div>
+    </div>
+  );
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/row-heights.ts b/src/components/data-grid/row-heights.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..312c4b9
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/row-heights.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,36 @@
+import type { TableVariant } from '../table/Table';
+import type { DataGridDensity } from './types';
+
+/**
+ * The height of a data row in pixels, by density and variant (spec §4.3). A row has no vertical
+ * padding in the grid, so this is the whole of it: the tallest content it usually holds (an
+ * Avatar `sm`, 24px) plus the padding a Table of that size has, plus the 1px rule of `lined`. It
+ * is the one copy of the table: the grid writes it to the root as `--flg-data-grid-row-height`,
+ * and the stylesheet reads it from there.
+ */
+export const ROW_HEIGHT: Readonly<Record<DataGridDensity, Readonly<Record<TableVariant, number>>>> =
+  {
+    compact: { lined: 31, striped: 30, minimal: 36 },
+    standard: { lined: 41, striped: 40, minimal: 52 },
+    comfortable: { lined: 49, striped: 48, minimal: 60 },
+  };
+
+/**
+ * The distance between the tops of two neighbouring rows: the height, and for `striped` the 2px
+ * its rows are apart. What a virtual window multiplies by before it has measured a real one.
+ */
+export function rowPitch(height: number, variant: TableVariant): number {
+  return variant === 'striped' ? height + 2 : height;
+}
+
+const DENSITIES = Object.keys(ROW_HEIGHT) as DataGridDensity[];
+const VARIANTS: readonly TableVariant[] = ['lined', 'striped', 'minimal'];
+
+// A value outside a union is the default; looking it up in the list narrows it without a cast.
+export function resolveDensity(value: unknown): DataGridDensity {
+  return DENSITIES.find((density) => density === value) ?? 'standard';
+}
+
+export function resolveVariant(value: unknown): TableVariant {
+  return VARIANTS.find((variant) => variant === value) ?? 'lined';
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/row-keys.ts b/src/components/data-grid/row-keys.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..6e32040
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/row-keys.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,62 @@
+import { devWarn, isProduction } from '../../internal/warn';
+import type { DataGridKey } from './types';
+
+/** The `rowKey` prop: the name of a property of the row, or a function of the row. */
+export type RowKey<TRow> = (keyof TRow & string) | ((row: TRow) => DataGridKey);
+
+/** What `rowKey` gives for a row, as it is: not yet known to be usable. */
+export function readRowKey<TRow>(rowKey: RowKey<TRow>, row: TRow): unknown {
+  if (typeof rowKey === 'function') return rowKey(row);
+  return typeof row === 'object' && row !== null
+    ? (row as Record<string, unknown>)[rowKey]
+    : undefined;
+}
+
+/** A key is a string or a finite number; anything else, `null` and `undefined` included, is not one. */
+export function usableKey(raw: unknown): DataGridKey | undefined {
+  if (typeof raw === 'string') return raw;
+  if (typeof raw === 'number' && Number.isFinite(raw)) return raw;
+  return undefined;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The React keys of a list of rows. A key that comes again is numbered (`a`, `a#2`), so React draws
+ * every row even when the data holds the same key twice (the grid warns about that); selection and
+ * focus, which go by the key itself, treat such rows as one. A number is written as the string React
+ * would make of it, so `1` and `"1"` are one key, and a numbered key never meets a real one.
+ */
+export function uniqueKeys(keys: readonly DataGridKey[]): string[] {
+  const seen = new Set<string>();
+  return keys.map((key) => {
+    const base = String(key);
+    let candidate = base;
+    for (let n = 2; seen.has(candidate); n++) candidate = `${base}#${n}`;
+    seen.add(candidate);
+    return candidate;
+  });
+}
+
+/**
+ * Development only: warns, once each, when a row has no usable key and when two rows have the
+ * same one. Run when `data` changes; in production the rows are not read at all.
+ */
+export function checkKeys<TRow>(data: readonly TRow[], rowKey: RowKey<TRow>): void {
+  if (isProduction()) return;
+  const seen = new Set<DataGridKey>();
+  let missing = false;
+  let repeated = false;
+  for (const row of data) {
+    const key = usableKey(readRowKey(rowKey, row));
+    if (key === undefined) missing = true;
+    else if (seen.has(key)) repeated = true;
+    else seen.add(key);
+  }
+  if (missing) {
+    devWarn(
+      '<DataGrid> a row has no usable key (rowKey gave something that is not a string or a number); its place in the list is used.',
+    );
+  }
+  if (repeated) {
+    devWarn('<DataGrid> two rows have the same key; selection and focus treat them as one row.');
+  }
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/types.ts b/src/components/data-grid/types.ts
index cd23f4a..ec32157 100644
--- a/src/components/data-grid/types.ts
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/types.ts
@@ -1,4 +1,5 @@
-import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
+import type { HTMLAttributes, ReactNode } from 'react';
+import type { TableVariant } from '../table/Table';
 
 /** What a row is known by: a string or a number, as the `key` of a React element. */
 export type DataGridKey = string | number;
@@ -90,3 +91,57 @@ export type DataGridValueColumn<TRow, V = unknown> = DataGridColumnBase<TRow, V>
 // `any` here is deliberate: a column list holds columns of different `V`.
 // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
 export type DataGridColumn<TRow> = DataGridFieldColumn<TRow> | DataGridValueColumn<TRow, any>;
+
+export type DataGridDensity = 'compact' | 'standard' | 'comfortable';
+
+/**
+ * Every word the grid says that is not the caller's: hidden text, and later the names of its
+ * controls and what it announces. All of them have an English default.
+ */
+export interface DataGridLabels {
+  /** The words of a boolean `true`, hidden next to its check, and of a `false`. */
+  yes: string;
+  no: string;
+}
+
+// The root always has children of its own, so `children` and `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (which may
+// not go with children) are not props; `onChange` is left to the controlled state of later plans.
+// This is an object type, so an app can `extend` it.
+export type DataGridProps<TRow> = Omit<
+  HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>,
+  'children' | 'onChange' | 'dangerouslySetInnerHTML'
+> & {
+  /** The rows. Rows are read, never changed; a changed row is a new object. */
+  data: readonly TRow[];
+  /** The key of a row: the name of a property, or a function of the row. Keys must be unique. */
+  rowKey: (keyof TRow & string) | ((row: TRow) => DataGridKey);
+  /** The columns. A stable array: a module constant or `useMemo`, not one written in the JSX. */
+  columns: readonly DataGridColumn<TRow>[];
+  /** The title of the grid, shown above it; it is the grid's name. */
+  caption?: ReactNode;
+  /** What the grid is about, under the caption; it describes the grid. */
+  description?: ReactNode;
+  captionAs?: 'h2' | 'h3' | 'h4' | 'h5' | 'h6' | 'div';
+  variant?: TableVariant;
+  density?: DataGridDensity;
+  /** The height of a row in pixels, over the one the density and variant give. */
+  rowHeight?: number;
+  /** The language of the numbers, dates and order of the text; `'en-US'` when left out. */
+  locale?: string;
+  /** The zone a `datetime` column is shown in; `'UTC'` when left out. */
+  timeZone?: string;
+  /**
+   * The height of the whole grid: a number of pixels or any CSS length. With a height the rows
+   * scroll under a heading that stays in place; without one the grid is as tall as its rows.
+   */
+  height?: number | string;
+  /** A class for the row of a data row. */
+  rowClassName?: (row: TRow) => string | undefined;
+  labels?: Partial<DataGridLabels>;
+};
+
+/** What a ref to a `DataGrid` holds: the grid's commands, not an element. */
+export interface DataGridHandle {
+  /** The element the grid is drawn in, `null` before it is mounted. */
+  readonly element: HTMLDivElement | null;
+}

diff --git a/src/styles/components/data-grid.css b/src/styles/components/data-grid.css
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..392b039
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/styles/components/data-grid.css
@@ -0,0 +1,143 @@
+/* DataGrid (spec phase 6 §3.7, §4.3 G1): rows of data in a Table's frame. The grid draws its rows with
+   the classes of Table (`flg-table-frame`, `flg-table`, `flg-table-head`, `flg-table-cell`…), so the
+   look of a variant, a size, a hover and a chosen row is Table's own and is not written again here.
+   What is here is what the grid adds: the row heights, the layout of the frame, and what Table's
+   rules would get wrong for a row that is drawn by a window and not by the markup. A rule here that
+   overrides one of Table's is as specific as it and later (this file is imported after table.css),
+   and says so. */
+@layer flg.components {
+  /* The root is a column: the caption, the grid, and later the pager. With a `height` the frame takes
+     what the caption and the pager leave and scrolls inside it. */
+  .flg-data-grid {
+    /* The height of a data row. The grid writes the one of its density and variant on its own `style`
+       (row-heights.ts holds the table, and a test holds the two equal); this is only what an element
+       without that style, a grid drawn by hand, reads. It is declared on the root so that a grid in a
+       cell of another never takes the outer one's. */
+    --flg-data-grid-row-height: 41px;
+    display: flex;
+    flex-direction: column;
+    gap: 14px;
+    min-width: 0;
+  }
+
+  /* The caption block, as the header of a Card (its own classes): the title and the description in a
+     column. It takes the room of the row and may be narrower than its text. */
+  .flg-data-grid-toolbar {
+    display: flex;
+    flex-wrap: wrap;
+    align-items: center;
+    gap: 8px;
+    min-width: 0;
+  }
+  .flg-data-grid-caption {
+    flex: 1 1 auto;
+    min-width: 0;
+  }
+
+  /* The main part is the frame and, later, what sits on it. It and the frame fill what is left of a
+     root that has a height, and may shrink below their content: that is what lets the frame scroll. */
+  .flg-data-grid-main {
+    display: flex;
+    flex-direction: column;
+    flex: 1 1 auto;
+    min-height: 0;
+    min-width: 0;
+  }
+  .flg-data-grid-frame {
+    /* The width the columns share, which the grid measures and writes here when a column is flexible
+       (the width of what spans every column follows it). Declared here and not left to inherit, so a
+       grid in a cell takes its own. */
+    --flg-data-grid-frame-width: 100%;
+    /* The height of the sticky heading, for the frame's scroll padding. The grid writes the measured
+       one when it has a height; until then, and for a grid in a cell of another, which would inherit
+       the outer one's, this is the estimate Table uses for a one-row heading of text. */
+    --flg-table-head-height: calc(2 * var(--flg-table-hpy) + 1.25rem);
+    flex: 1 1 auto;
+    min-height: 0;
+  }
+
+  /* Every column has a `<col>`, so the widths are the ones the grid says and the text of a cell
+     cannot widen its column. */
+  .flg-data-grid-table {
+    table-layout: fixed;
+  }
+
+  /* A heading cell: the title in a row that holds, later, its buttons. A title that is too long ends
+     in an ellipsis; a column of numbers has its title at the end (Table's own `data-align`). */
+  .flg-data-grid-head-content {
+    display: flex;
+    align-items: center;
+    gap: 4px;
+    min-width: 0;
+  }
+  .flg-data-grid-head-content > * {
+    min-width: 0;
+    overflow: hidden;
+    text-overflow: ellipsis;
+  }
+  .flg-data-grid-head[data-align='end'] .flg-data-grid-head-content {
+    flex-direction: row-reverse;
+  }
+  .flg-data-grid-head[data-align='center'] .flg-data-grid-head-content {
+    justify-content: center;
+  }
+
+  /* A data row has the height of the grid and its cells no padding above or below: the cell is as
+     tall as the row and centres what is in it, so the height does not depend on the content (which a
+     virtual window needs). The padding at the sides is Table's. The text is cut with an ellipsis. */
+  .flg-data-grid-row {
+    height: var(--flg-data-grid-row-height);
+  }
+  .flg-data-grid-table .flg-data-grid-cell {
+    padding-block: 0;
+    overflow: hidden;
+    text-overflow: ellipsis;
+  }
+  /* The check of a boolean that is true. The colour is on the span and not on the <svg>, which keeps
+     a colour set on it in forced colours (Table's sort icon does the same). */
+  .flg-data-grid-check {
+    display: inline-flex;
+    vertical-align: middle;
+    color: var(--flg-accent-text);
+  }
+
+  /* The heading sticks as a whole and is above the cells that scroll and, later, those that are pinned.
+     Table's rule has the same selector and `z-index: 1`; this one is later. */
+  .flg-data-grid-frame[data-sticky-header] .flg-table-header {
+    z-index: 2;
+  }
+  /* The cells of a sticky heading are painted over a solid colour that is not the 94% tint Table
+     uses: the rows that scroll under it showed through in the other 6%. Same selector as Table's
+     rule for it, and later. Forced colours and more contrast make it `Canvas` in preferences.css. */
+  .flg-data-grid-frame[data-sticky-header] .flg-table-header :is(.flg-table-head, .flg-table-cell) {
+    background:
+      linear-gradient(var(--flg-table-head-bg), var(--flg-table-head-bg)),
+      var(--flg-data-grid-pin-bg);
+  }
+
+  /* The stripes of `striped` are on the rows that say so (`data-stripe`) and not on Table's odd
+     children, because a window that adds and drops rows at its top would move them. Table's stripe
+     is turned off on a row of the grid, then drawn again where `data-stripe` is; both have the
+     specificity of Table's rule (six classes) and come later. A row under the pointer is painted
+     again after them, since the first of these would otherwise take its hover from an odd row. */
+  .flg-data-grid-frame[data-variant='striped']
+    .flg-table-body
+    > .flg-data-grid-row:not([data-selected]):nth-child(odd)
+    > * {
+    background: none;
+  }
+  .flg-data-grid-frame[data-variant='striped']
+    .flg-table-body
+    > .flg-data-grid-row[data-stripe]:not([data-selected])
+    > * {
+    background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--flg-control-track) 50%, transparent);
+  }
+  @media (hover: hover) {
+    .flg-data-grid-frame[data-variant='striped']
+      .flg-table-body
+      > .flg-data-grid-row:not([data-selected]):hover
+      > * {
+      background: var(--flg-control-track);
+    }
+  }
+}

+
+// What a press on a title does is read from the grid: the ids in the order of the rows, the order of a
+// column as numbers, and the sort the headings say.
+const idsIn = (root: HTMLElement) =>
+  Array.from(root.querySelectorAll('tbody > tr > th')).map((cell) => cell.textContent);
+const columnIn = (root: HTMLElement, index: number) =>
+  Array.from(root.querySelectorAll('tbody > tr')).map((row) =>
+    Number((row.children[index] as HTMLElement).textContent!.replace(/\D/g, '')),
+  );
+const headOf = (root: HTMLElement, caption: string) =>
+  Array.from(root.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('thead th')).find((th) =>
+    th.textContent?.startsWith(caption),
+  )!;
+const titleOf = (root: HTMLElement, caption: string) =>
+  within(headOf(root, caption)).getByRole('button');
+type Real = NonNullable<Awaited<ReturnType<typeof realUserEvent>>>;
+
+/**
+ * Runs a press and says whether the `mousedown` of it was cancelled. The listener is on the document,
+ * after React's, so it sees what the grid's handler did. A cancelled `mousedown` is what keeps the
+ * browser from starting a text selection (and from moving the focus) with a Shift press.
+ */
+async function cancelledMouseDown(press: () => Promise<void>): Promise<boolean> {
+  const seen: boolean[] = [];
+  const watch = (event: MouseEvent) => seen.push(event.defaultPrevented);
+  document.addEventListener('mousedown', watch);
+  try {
+    await press();
+  } finally {
+    document.removeEventListener('mousedown', watch);
+  }
+  await expect(seen).toHaveLength(1);
+  return seen[0]!;
+}
+
+/** A press with a modifier held, as the browser sees it: the key goes down, the press, the key up. */
+async function pressWith(real: Real, key: 'Shift' | 'Meta' | 'Control', element: HTMLElement) {
+  await real.keyboard(`{${key}>}`);
+  try {
+    return await cancelledMouseDown(() => real.click(element));
+  } finally {
+    await real.keyboard(`{/${key}}`);
+  }
+}
+
+/**
+ * A press on a title sorts: ascending, then descending, then back to the order of the data. A press
+ * with Shift adds a level, and that press does not select text. To prove the last, a caret is put in
+ * a cell first: Shift with a press on something else is what extends a selection from the caret to it,
+ * unless the `mousedown` is cancelled.
+ */
+export const Sorting: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  render: () => (
+    <DataGrid data={ORDERS.slice(0, 8)} rowKey="id" columns={COLUMNS} caption="Orders" />
+  ),
+  play: async ({ canvasElement, canvas }) => {
+    const real = await realUserEvent();
+    if (!real) return;
+    const original = idsIn(canvasElement);
+    await real.click(titleOf(canvasElement, 'Qty'));
+    await expect(headOf(canvasElement, 'Qty')).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'ascending');
+    const ascending = columnIn(canvasElement, 3);
+    await expect(ascending).toEqual([...ascending].sort((a, b) => a - b));
+    await expect(ascending[0]).toBeLessThan(ascending.at(-1)!);
+    await real.click(titleOf(canvasElement, 'Qty'));
+    await expect(headOf(canvasElement, 'Qty')).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'descending');
+    const descending = columnIn(canvasElement, 3);
+    await expect(descending).toEqual([...descending].sort((a, b) => b - a));
+    await real.click(titleOf(canvasElement, 'Qty'));
+    await expect(headOf(canvasElement, 'Qty')).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-sort');
+    await expect(idsIn(canvasElement)).toEqual(original);
+
+    // Two levels: Qty, then Total inside equal quantities.
+    // A plain press leaves its `mousedown` alone; one that adds a level cancels it.
+    await expect(cancelledMouseDown(() => real.click(titleOf(canvasElement, 'Qty')))).resolves.toBe(
+      false,
+    );
+    await real.click(canvas.getAllByRole('rowheader')[0]!);
+    await expect(pressWith(real, 'Shift', titleOf(canvasElement, 'Total'))).resolves.toBe(true);
+    await expect(window.getSelection()?.toString()).toBe('');
+    await expect(canvasElement.querySelectorAll('.flg-data-grid-sort-index')).toHaveLength(2);
+    await expect(titleOf(canvasElement, 'Total')).toHaveAccessibleName(
+      // A browser may put a space before the comma, where the hidden words begin.
+      /^Total\s*, sorted ascending, 2 of 2$/,
+    );
+    // Only the first level has aria-sort.
+    await expect(headOf(canvasElement, 'Total')).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-sort');
+    await expect(headOf(canvasElement, 'Qty')).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'ascending');
+  },
+};
+
+// The stories below are written out, not made by a function: the tags and the play function of a
+// story are read from the file without running it.
+const modifierPlay =
+  (key: 'Meta' | 'Control'): NonNullable<Story['play']> =>
+  async ({ canvasElement }) => {
+    const real = await realUserEvent();
+    if (!real) return;
+    await real.click(titleOf(canvasElement, 'Qty'));
+    await expect(pressWith(real, key, titleOf(canvasElement, 'Total'))).resolves.toBe(true);
+    // The key that is the modifier of this platform adds a level, and the press leaves no selection.
+    await expect(canvasElement.querySelectorAll('.flg-data-grid-sort-index')).toHaveLength(2);
+    await expect(window.getSelection()?.toString()).toBe('');
+    // The same press turns the level, then takes it off.
+    await expect(pressWith(real, key, titleOf(canvasElement, 'Total'))).resolves.toBe(true);
+    await expect(titleOf(canvasElement, 'Total')).toHaveAccessibleName(
+      /^Total\s*, sorted descending, 2 of 2$/,
+    );
+    await expect(pressWith(real, key, titleOf(canvasElement, 'Total'))).resolves.toBe(true);
+    await expect(canvasElement.querySelectorAll('.flg-data-grid-sort-index')).toHaveLength(0);
+    await expect(headOf(canvasElement, 'Qty')).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'ascending');
+  };
+
+const ModifierGrid = () => (
+  <DataGrid data={ORDERS.slice(0, 8)} rowKey="id" columns={COLUMNS} caption="Orders" />
+);
+
+/** The modifier that adds a level is ⌘ on an Apple system. */
+export const SortingModifierApple: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  beforeEach: onPlatform('apple'),
+  render: () => <ModifierGrid />,
+  play: modifierPlay('Meta'),
+};
+
+/** And Ctrl on any other. */
+export const SortingModifierOther: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  beforeEach: onPlatform('other'),
+  render: () => <ModifierGrid />,
+  play: modifierPlay('Control'),
+};
+
+/**
+ * The pager moves between pages, and a choice of size keeps the first row that is shown: the second
+ * page of 10 starts at the eleventh row, which is the first of the page of 20.
+ */
+export const Paging: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  render: () => (
+    <DataGrid
+      data={ORDERS}
+      rowKey="id"
+      columns={COLUMNS}
+      caption="Orders"
+      paging={{ pageSize: 10, pageSizes: [10, 20] }}
+    />
+  ),
+  play: async ({ canvasElement, canvas }) => {
+    const real = await realUserEvent();
+    if (!real) return;
+    const info = () => canvasElement.querySelector('.flg-data-grid-page-info')!.textContent;
+    await expect(info()).toBe('1–10 of 40');
+    await expect(canvasElement.querySelectorAll('tbody > tr')).toHaveLength(10);
+    await real.click(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Page 2' }));
+    await expect(info()).toBe('11–20 of 40');
+    await expect(idsIn(canvasElement)[0]).toBe(ORDERS[10]!.id);
+    await real.click(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Next page' }));
+    await expect(info()).toBe('21–30 of 40');
+    await real.click(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Page 2' }));
+    const trigger = canvas.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Rows per page' });
+    await expect(trigger).toHaveTextContent('10 / page');
+    await real.click(trigger);
+    const listbox = canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-select-listbox')!;
+    await real.click(within(listbox).getByRole('option', { name: '20 / page' }));
+    await waitFor(() => expect(trigger).toHaveTextContent('20 / page'));
+    await expect(canvasElement.querySelectorAll('tbody > tr')).toHaveLength(20);
+    await expect(info()).toBe('1–20 of 40');
+    await expect(idsIn(canvasElement)[0]).toBe(ORDERS[0]!.id);
+  },
+};
+
+/**
+ * In server mode the data is the page and is already in order: a press on a title shows the sort in
+ * the heading and calls `onSortChange`, and the rows stay where they are; the pager counts
+ * `totalCount` and calls `onPageChange`.
+ */
+export const ServerMode: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  args: {
+    data: ORDERS.slice(0, 10),
+    columns: COLUMNS,
+    remote: true,
+    totalCount: 135,
+    paging: { pageSize: 10, pageSizes: [10, 20] },
+    caption: 'Orders',
+    onSortChange: fn(),
+    onPageChange: fn(),
+    onStateChange: fn(),
+  },
+  play: async ({ canvasElement, canvas, args }) => {
+    const real = await realUserEvent();
+    if (!real) return;
+    const original = idsIn(canvasElement);
+    const info = () => canvasElement.querySelector('.flg-data-grid-page-info')!.textContent;
+    await real.click(titleOf(canvasElement, 'Qty'));
+    await expect(args.onSortChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+    await expect(args.onSortChange).toHaveBeenCalledWith([{ field: 'qty', direction: 'asc' }]);
+    await expect(headOf(canvasElement, 'Qty')).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'ascending');
+    await expect(idsIn(canvasElement)).toEqual(original);
+    await expect(info()).toBe('1–10 of 135');
+    await real.click(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Page 2' }));
+    await expect(args.onPageChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+    await expect(args.onPageChange).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ index: 1, size: 10 });
+    await expect(args.onStateChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(
+      { sort: [{ field: 'qty', direction: 'asc' }], page: { index: 1, size: 10 } },
+      'page',
+    );
+    await expect(idsIn(canvasElement)).toEqual(original);
+    await expect(info()).toBe('11–20 of 135');
+  },
+};

+// What JSON can carry, so an app can keep the state in `localStorage` or send it to a server.
+type IsJson<T> = T extends string | number | boolean | null
+  ? true
+  : T extends readonly (infer Item)[]
+    ? IsJson<Item>
+    : T extends object
+      ? { [K in keyof T]: IsJson<T[K]> }[keyof T] extends true
+        ? true
+        : false
+      : false;
+
+test('the state of the grid is JSON only, and onStateChange names the part that changed', () => {
+  expectTypeOf<IsJson<DataGridState>>().toEqualTypeOf<true>();
+  expectTypeOf<keyof DataGridState>().toEqualTypeOf<'sort' | 'page'>();
+  expectTypeOf<DataGridProps<Order>['onStateChange']>().toEqualTypeOf<
+    ((state: DataGridState, changed: keyof DataGridState) => void) | undefined
+  >();
+  expectTypeOf<DataGridHandle['getState']>().toEqualTypeOf<() => DataGridState>();
+});
+
+test('sorting, paging and server mode props take only their own values', () => {
+  expectTypeOf<DataGridProps<Order>['sortMode']>().toEqualTypeOf<
+    'single' | 'multiple' | undefined
+  >();
+  expectTypeOf<DataGridProps<Order>['paging']>().toEqualTypeOf<
+    false | { pageSize?: number; pageSizes?: readonly number[] } | undefined
+  >();
+  // @ts-expect-error not a sort mode
+  const mode: DataGridProps<Order>['sortMode'] = 'some';
+  void mode;
+});

+  });
+
+  it('draws the title in a button with the arrow of its direction, and the chevrons before', () => {

+describe('announcing a sort', () => {

+## Sorting
+
+A column whose title is a button sorts. A press makes that column the only sort: ascending, then
+descending, then no sort, which puts the rows back in the order of `data`. A press with Shift, or
+with ⌘ on an Apple system and Ctrl on any other, adds the column as another level, and a second such
+press turns it and a third takes it off, so that "Order date, then Total" is two presses. The keys
+`Enter` and `Shift+Enter` on a button do the same. A press with a modifier does not select text.
+
+```tsx
+<DataGrid
+  data={orders}
+  rowKey="id"
+  columns={columns}
+  defaultSort={[{ field: 'date', direction: 'desc' }]}
+/>
+```
+
+<Canvas of={Stories.Sorting} />
+
+- **Which columns.** `allowSorting` is the default of every column (`true`), and a column's own
+  `allowSorting` wins. A column that does not sort has a plain title: no button and no arrow, since
+  an arrow would promise a control. `sortMode="single"` keeps one column: the modifiers do nothing.
+- **How they compare.** Text with `Intl.Collator` in the grid's `locale`, with `numeric`, so "DH-2"
+  comes before "DH-10"; numbers, dates and booleans as numbers; a column with a `lookup` by the text
+  it shows. `sortValue(row)` replaces the value that the column is sorted by. A blank value is last,
+  whichever way the column sorts, and rows that are equal keep their order.
+- **What a screen reader gets.** `aria-sort` is on the heading of the first level only, since a table
+  has one sorted column at a time. With more than one column sorted, every sorted title also says its
+  place in hidden words, ", sorted descending, 2 of 3" (`labels.sortState`), and the number is drawn
+  next to the arrow and hidden from a screen reader. After a press the grid says the whole sort,
+  "Sorted by Order date, descending, then Total, ascending", or "Sorting cleared"
+  (`labels.announceSort`, `labels.announceSortCleared`). It says nothing on mount, and nothing when a
+  controlled `sort` changes from outside.
+- **A sort that is no longer true.** An item of `sort` whose `field` is not a column that sorts, or
+  whose direction is not `'asc'` or `'desc'`, is left out without a warning: the state may come from
+  what a person saved before the columns changed.
+
+## Paging
+
+The grid pages by default: `paging` is `{ pageSize: 20, pageSizes: [10, 20, 50, 100] }`. Under the
+rows there is a bar with the count ("1–20 of 135"), the choice of how many rows a page holds, and
+the pages. `paging={false}` is one page of every row and no bar. The bar is not drawn when there are
+no rows. A page is counted from 0: `{ index: 0, size: 20 }` is the first.
+
+<Canvas of={Stories.Paging} />
+
+- **The choice of size** lists `pageSizes` and the size in use if it is not among them, in order,
+  once each. Pass `pageSizes: []` for no choice.
+- **A new size** keeps the first row that is shown: from the third page of 20, a size of 10 goes to
+  the fifth page, whose first row is the row that was first. That is one `onPageChange`.
+- **Sorting keeps the page.** A page that is out of range, because the data shrank or the state
+  came from storage, is drawn as the nearest one, and no callback is called for that.
+- **The name of the pages** is `labels.pagination` and the caption read together ("Pagination
+  Orders"), so two captioned grids on a page have two landmarks that differ. A grid without a caption
+  has `labels.pagination` alone: give each such grid its own.
+- **`paging={false}` leaves the page state as it is held**, unused: `getState().page` is still
+  `{ index: 0, size: 20 }` (or your controlled value), and it does not change when the data does. A
+  state saved with paging off and restored with paging on behaves as `paging` says.
+
+## Server mode
+
+With `remote` the grid sorts and pages nothing: `data` is the page, already in order, and the grid
+draws it as it is. It counts `totalCount` rows in the bar, and a press on a title or on a page calls
+`onSortChange` or `onPageChange` for you to load again. The header still shows the sort the press
+asked for, and an uncontrolled sort and page are kept, so a grid that you do not control still
+moves. Without `totalCount` the rows of `data` are counted, and the grid warns once.
+
+<Canvas of={Stories.ServerMode} />
+
+What the grid does not do in server mode: it does not sort or page `data`, and it cannot know
+whether `data` is in the order its heading says. That is for the server to keep true.
+
+## State
+
+The sort and the page are each a controlled or an uncontrolled value, as every field of the library:
+`sort`, `defaultSort` and `onSortChange`; `page`, `defaultPage` and `onPageChange`. A controlled
+value that you do not take stays as it was, and the callback still hears the press.
+
+`onStateChange(state, changed)` is called after `onSortChange` or `onPageChange` with the whole state
+that the press asks for, `{ sort, page }`, and the name of the part that changed, so that one
+function can save the state of the grid. It is called from what a person does, never from a render:
+a controlled value that you change from outside does not call it. The state holds only what JSON can
+carry, so it can go to `localStorage` or to a server and come back as `defaultSort` and
+`defaultPage`.
+
+`ref.current.getState()` returns the state the grid shows: the same, but with the page as drawn.
+

+/**
+ * The items that sort, in their order: an item whose field is not a column that sorts, or whose
+ * direction is not `asc` or `desc`, or whose field came before, is dropped without a word, since a
+ * state may come from the end user's storage (spec phase 6 §5). The first item of a field wins.
+ */
+export function effectiveSort<TRow>(
+  items: readonly DataGridSortItem[],
+  columns: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[],
+): DataGridSortItem[] {
+  const kept: DataGridSortItem[] = [];
+  for (const item of items) {
+    const column = columns.find((candidate) => candidate.id === item.field);
+    if (!column?.allowSorting) continue;
+    if (item.direction !== 'asc' && item.direction !== 'desc') continue;
+    if (kept.some((other) => other.field === item.field)) continue;
+    kept.push({ field: item.field, direction: item.direction });
+  }
+  return kept;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The sort after a press on the title of `field`. A plain press makes the column the only sort, at
+ * its next direction (not sorted, ascending, descending, not sorted). A press that adds (Shift, or
+ * ⌘ or Ctrl) keeps the other columns and adds this one ascending, turns it where it is, or removes
+ * it after descending. In `'single'` mode the press never adds. The items are the effective ones
+ * (`effectiveSort`); a new array comes back and the one that came in is not changed.
+ */
+export function nextSort(
+  items: readonly DataGridSortItem[],
+  field: string,
+  additive: boolean,
+  sortMode: DataGridSortMode,
+): DataGridSortItem[] {
+  const current = items.find((item) => item.field === field)?.direction;
+  const next = current === undefined ? 'asc' : current === 'asc' ? 'desc' : undefined;
+  if (!additive || sortMode === 'single') return next ? [{ field, direction: next }] : [];
+  if (current === undefined) return [...items, { field, direction: 'asc' }];
+  return next
+    ? items.map((item) => (item.field === field ? { field, direction: next } : item))
+    : items.filter((item) => item.field !== field);
+}

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..c754317
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-grid-state.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,95 @@
+import { useCallback, useMemo, useRef } from 'react';
+import { useControllableState } from '../../../internal/use-controllable-state';
+import { useWriteOnCommit } from '../../../internal/use-write-on-commit';
+import type { DataGridPage, DataGridSortItem, DataGridState } from '../types';
+
+const NO_SORT: readonly DataGridSortItem[] = [];
+
+export interface GridStateOptions {
+  sort: readonly DataGridSortItem[] | undefined;
+  defaultSort: readonly DataGridSortItem[] | undefined;
+  onSortChange: ((sort: readonly DataGridSortItem[]) => void) | undefined;
+  page: DataGridPage | undefined;
+  /** What the page is until the user moves it: `defaultPage`, or the first page of the usual size. */
+  defaultPage: DataGridPage;
+  onPageChange: ((page: DataGridPage) => void) | undefined;
+  onStateChange: ((state: DataGridState, changed: keyof DataGridState) => void) | undefined;
+}
+
+export interface GridState {
+  /** The state as the app holds it, or as the grid does while it is uncontrolled. */
+  state: DataGridState;
+  /** Asks for a sort: `onSortChange`, then `onStateChange`; an uncontrolled sort is kept. */
+  setSort: (sort: readonly DataGridSortItem[]) => void;
+  /** Asks for a page, the same way; the page that is already asked for is not reported. */
+  setPage: (page: DataGridPage) => void;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The state of the sort and of the page, each a controllable triple (`value`, `defaultValue`,
+ * `onChange`), and `onStateChange` after each of them with the whole state. A controlled value is
+ * reported too, since the parent may reject it: the state sent is what the press asks for, and the
+ * grid goes on showing the parent's. Nothing is called from a render or an effect: only the setters
+ * call, and only event handlers call the setters.
+ */
+export function useGridState({
+  sort,
+  defaultSort,
+  onSortChange,
+  page,
+  defaultPage,
+  onPageChange,
+  onStateChange,
+}: GridStateOptions): GridState {
+  const [sortValue, setSortValue] = useControllableState<readonly DataGridSortItem[]>({
+    value: sort,
+    defaultValue: defaultSort ?? NO_SORT,
+    onChange: onSortChange,
+    name: 'DataGrid sort',
+  });
+  const [pageValue, setPageValue] = useControllableState<DataGridPage>({
+    value: page,
+    defaultValue: defaultPage,
+    onChange: onPageChange,
+    name: 'DataGrid page',
+  });
+  const state = useMemo(() => ({ sort: sortValue, page: pageValue }), [sortValue, pageValue]);
+
+  // What the setters read: the state of the last commit, and which parts the parent owns. An
+  // uncontrolled part is also written by the setter, so two requests in one event see each other.
+  const latest = useRef({ state, sortOwned: false, pageOwned: false, onStateChange });
+  useWriteOnCommit(() => {
+    latest.current = {
+      state,
+      sortOwned: sort !== undefined,
+      pageOwned: page !== undefined,
+      onStateChange,
+    };
+  });
+
+  const setSort = useCallback(
+    (next: readonly DataGridSortItem[]) => {
+      const before = latest.current;
+      setSortValue(next);
+      const asked = { ...before.state, sort: next };
+      if (!before.sortOwned) latest.current = { ...before, state: asked };
+      before.onStateChange?.(asked, 'sort');
+    },
+    [setSortValue],
+  );
+
+  const setPage = useCallback(
+    (next: DataGridPage) => {
+      const before = latest.current;
+      const now = before.state.page;
+      if (now.index === next.index && now.size === next.size) return;
+      setPageValue(next);
+      const asked = { ...before.state, page: next };
+      if (!before.pageOwned) latest.current = { ...before, state: asked };
+      before.onStateChange?.(asked, 'page');
+    },
+    [setPageValue],
+  );
+
+  return { state, setSort, setPage };
+}

index 0000000..b1ef6bc
--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,77 @@
+import { useId } from 'react';
+import { Pagination } from '../../pagination/Pagination';
+import { Select, SelectItem } from '../../select/Select';
+import type { DataGridLabels } from '../types';
+
+interface PagerProps {
+  labels: DataGridLabels;
+  /** The id of the grid's caption, when it has one: it is part of the name of the pages. */
+  captionId: string | undefined;
+  /** The page shown, counted from 0, and how many pages there are. */
+  pageIndex: number;
+  pageCount: number;
+  /** How many rows a page holds, and how many rows there are in all. */
+  size: number;
+  total: number;
+  /** The sizes the user may choose, ascending; none means no choice. */
+  sizes: readonly number[];
+  onPage: (index: number) => void;
+  onSize: (size: number) => void;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The bar under the grid: the count, the choice of how many rows a page holds, and the pages. The
+ * parts are the library's own, so their look and their keys are theirs.
+ */
+export function Pager({
+  labels,
+  captionId,
+  pageIndex,
+  pageCount,
+  size,
+  total,
+  sizes,
+  onPage,
+  onSize,
+}: PagerProps) {
+  const nameId = useId();
+  const from = pageIndex * size + 1;
+  const to = Math.min(total, from + size - 1);
+  return (
+    <div className="flg-data-grid-pager">
+      <span className="flg-data-grid-page-info">{labels.pageInfo(from, to, total)}</span>
+      {sizes.length > 0 ? (
+        <Select
+          size="sm"
+          className="flg-data-grid-page-size"
+          aria-label={labels.rowsPerPage}
+          value={String(size)}
+          onValueChange={(value) => onSize(Number(value))}
+        >
+          {sizes.map((option) => (
+            <SelectItem key={option} value={String(option)}>
+              {labels.pageSize(option)}
+            </SelectItem>
+          ))}
+        </Select>
+      ) : null}
+      {/* With a caption the name is the two read together ("Pagination Orders"), so two grids on a
+          page have two landmarks that differ; without one it is `labels.pagination` alone. */}
+      {captionId ? (
+        <span id={nameId} hidden>
+          {labels.pagination}
+        </span>
+      ) : null}
+      <Pagination
+        count={pageCount}
+        page={pageIndex + 1}
+        onPageChange={(page) => onPage(page - 1)}
+        aria-label={captionId ? undefined : labels.pagination}
+        aria-labelledby={captionId ? `${nameId} ${captionId}` : undefined}
+        previousLabel={labels.previousPage}
+        nextLabel={labels.nextPage}
+        getPageLabel={labels.page}
+      />
+    </div>
+  );
+}
