diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/engine/selection.ts b/src/components/data-grid/engine/selection.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..e323702
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/engine/selection.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,80 @@
+import type { DataGridKey } from '../types';
+
+// What the grid does with the keys of the chosen rows (spec phase 6 §6.3, "Chọn dòng"). The keys
+// are kept as an array in the order they were chosen, because that is what an app saves (JSON has no
+// set); every function here gives a new array and never changes the one it was given.
+
+/** Whether two lists hold the same keys in the same order. A number is not the text of it. */
+export function sameKeys(a: readonly DataGridKey[], b: readonly DataGridKey[]): boolean {
+  return a.length === b.length && a.every((key, index) => key === b[index]);
+}
+
+/** The keys of `current` and then those of `add` that are not in it, once each. */
+export function addKeys(
+  current: readonly DataGridKey[],
+  add: readonly DataGridKey[],
+): DataGridKey[] {
+  const seen = new Set(current);
+  const next = [...current];
+  for (const key of add) {
+    if (!seen.has(key)) {
+      seen.add(key);
+      next.push(key);
+    }
+  }
+  return next;
+}
+
+/** The keys of `current` that are not in `remove`, in their order. */
+export function removeKeys(
+  current: readonly DataGridKey[],
+  remove: readonly DataGridKey[],
+): DataGridKey[] {
+  const gone = new Set(remove);
+  return current.filter((key) => !gone.has(key));
+}
+
+/** `current` without `key` when it has it, else with `key` last. */
+export function toggleKey(current: readonly DataGridKey[], key: DataGridKey): DataGridKey[] {
+  return current.includes(key) ? removeKeys(current, [key]) : [...current, key];
+}
+
+/**
+ * The rows from `anchor` to `to`, both included, in the order of `rows` whichever of them comes
+ * first. With no anchor, or one that is not among `rows`, or a row that is not, the range is `to`
+ * alone: there is nothing to span.
+ */
+export function rangeKeys(
+  rows: readonly { key: DataGridKey }[],
+  anchor: DataGridKey | null,
+  to: DataGridKey,
+): DataGridKey[] {
+  const from = anchor === null ? -1 : rows.findIndex((row) => row.key === anchor);
+  const end = rows.findIndex((row) => row.key === to);
+  if (from < 0 || end < 0) return [to];
+  const [first, last] = from <= end ? [from, end] : [end, from];
+  return rows.slice(first, last + 1).map((row) => row.key);
+}
+
+/** How much of a scope (the keys of the rows a "select all" is about) is chosen. */
+export interface ScopeState {
+  /** Every row of the scope is chosen, and there is one. */
+  checked: boolean;
+  /** Some rows of the scope are chosen, not all. */
+  indeterminate: boolean;
+  /** There are no rows in the scope: nothing to choose. */
+  disabled: boolean;
+}
+
+export function scopeState(
+  scope: readonly DataGridKey[],
+  chosen: ReadonlySet<DataGridKey> | readonly DataGridKey[],
+): ScopeState {
+  const set = chosen instanceof Set ? chosen : new Set(chosen);
+  const count = scope.filter((key) => set.has(key)).length;
+  return {
+    checked: scope.length > 0 && count === scope.length,
+    indeterminate: count > 0 && count < scope.length,
+    disabled: scope.length === 0,
+  };
+}

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..c570f0c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-selection.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,121 @@
+import { useCallback, useMemo, useRef } from 'react';
+import { useWriteOnCommit } from '../../../internal/use-write-on-commit';
+import type { FlatRow } from '../engine/flatten';
+import { addKeys, rangeKeys, removeKeys, scopeState, toggleKey } from '../engine/selection';
+import type { ScopeState } from '../engine/selection';
+import type {
+  DataGridKey,
+  DataGridLabels,
+  DataGridSelectAllMode,
+  DataGridSelectionMode,
+} from '../types';
+
+export interface SelectionOptions<TRow> {
+  mode: DataGridSelectionMode;
+  /** The scope of "select all", with server mode already counted in. */
+  allMode: DataGridSelectAllMode;
+  /** The chosen keys, as the grid holds them. */
+  keys: readonly DataGridKey[];
+  /** `useGridState`'s `setSelectedKeys`. */
+  setKeys: (
+    change: (current: readonly DataGridKey[]) => readonly DataGridKey[] | undefined,
+  ) => readonly DataGridKey[] | undefined;
+  /** The rows of the page that is shown, in order. */
+  pageRows: readonly FlatRow<TRow>[];
+  /** Every row after sorting, in order: the order a range is taken in, and the scope of `'all'`. */
+  orderedRows: readonly FlatRow<TRow>[];
+  labels: DataGridLabels;
+  announce: (text: string) => void;
+}
+
+/** What the rows and the title read of the selection: it changes with every choice. */
+export interface SelectionView {
+  /** The chosen keys as a set, for a row to ask whether it is chosen. */
+  chosen: ReadonlySet<DataGridKey>;
+  /** The box in the title: checked, mixed, or disabled when its scope is empty. */
+  header: ScopeState;
+}
+
+/**
+ * What a press or a key does. It is the same object for as long as the grid keeps its mode, and
+ * reads the rows and the words of the last commit when it is called, so a choice that changes one
+ * row does not give the other rows a new prop to draw again for.
+ */
+export interface SelectionActions {
+  /** A press on a row, or on its box: with `range` (Shift) it adds the rows from the anchor to it. */
+  press: (key: DataGridKey, range: boolean) => void;
+  /** The box in the title: the rows of the scope are chosen, or taken off. */
+  setAll: (checked: boolean) => void;
+  /** mod+A: every row of the scope is chosen. */
+  chooseAll: () => void;
+}
+
+function scopeKeys<TRow>({ allMode, pageRows, orderedRows }: SelectionOptions<TRow>) {
+  return (allMode === 'all' ? orderedRows : pageRows).map((row) => row.key);
+}
+
+/**
+ * Choosing rows (spec phase 6 §6.3, "Chọn dòng"). `single` replaces the choice; `multiple` toggles a
+ * row, adds a range from the anchor (the last row toggled by a plain press or Space), and chooses
+ * or takes off the scope of "select all". What is chosen is kept by key, so a sort, a page or a row
+ * that leaves the data does not change it. Only an event calls anything, never a render.
+ */
+export function useSelection<TRow>(options: SelectionOptions<TRow>): {
+  view: SelectionView;
+  actions: SelectionActions;
+} {
+  const { mode, keys, allMode, pageRows, orderedRows } = options;
+  const chosen = useMemo(() => new Set(keys), [keys]);
+  const scope = allMode === 'all' ? orderedRows : pageRows;
+  const header = useMemo(
+    () =>
+      scopeState(
+        scope.map((row) => row.key),
+        chosen,
+      ),
+    [scope, chosen],
+  );
+  const view = useMemo(() => ({ chosen, header }), [chosen, header]);
+
+  // What the actions read when they are called, written when a commit starts.
+  const latest = useRef(options);
+  useWriteOnCommit(() => {
+    latest.current = options;
+  });
+  // The row a range starts from: the last one a plain press or Space chose. No render shows it.
+  const anchor = useRef<DataGridKey | null>(null);
+
+  const press = useCallback(
+    (key: DataGridKey, range: boolean) => {
+      const { setKeys, orderedRows: ordered, announce, labels } = latest.current;
+      if (mode === 'single') {
+        anchor.current = key;
+        setKeys(() => [key]);
+      } else if (mode === 'multiple' && range) {
+        const next = setKeys((now) => addKeys(now, rangeKeys(ordered, anchor.current, key)));
+        if (next) announce(labels.announceSelected(next.length));
+      } else if (mode === 'multiple') {
+        anchor.current = key;
+        setKeys((now) => toggleKey(now, key));
+      }
+    },
+    [mode],
+  );
+
+  const setAll = useCallback((checked: boolean) => {
+    const { setKeys, announce, labels } = latest.current;
+    const ofScope = scopeKeys(latest.current);
+    const next = setKeys((now) => (checked ? addKeys(now, ofScope) : removeKeys(now, ofScope)));
+    if (checked && next) announce(labels.announceSelected(next.length));
+  }, []);
+
+  const chooseAll = useCallback(() => {
+    const { setKeys, announce, labels, keys: now } = latest.current;
+    const ofScope = scopeKeys(latest.current);
+    // Said even when every row of the scope was chosen already: whoever pressed the keys wants the count.
+    announce(labels.announceSelected((setKeys((held) => addKeys(held, ofScope)) ?? now).length));
+  }, []);
+
+  const actions = useMemo(() => ({ press, setAll, chooseAll }), [press, setAll, chooseAll]);
+  return { view, actions };
+}

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/parts/SelectCells.tsx b/src/components/data-grid/parts/SelectCells.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..03156dd
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/parts/SelectCells.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,71 @@
+import { useContext } from 'react';
+import { Checkbox } from '../../checkbox/Checkbox';
+import type { FlatRow } from '../engine/flatten';
+import { SelectionViewContext, useGridContext } from '../grid-context';
+
+/**
+ * The box of a row, in the column of boxes. The box is the focus target of its cell (the data grid
+ * pattern of the APG: a cell that holds one simple control gives the focus to it), so it is the Tab
+ * stop when this is the active cell, and the cell is never one.
+ *
+ * The press is read from the click of the box, which every way of pressing it makes once (a pointer,
+ * a press on its label, Enter), so that Shift is the click's own. A press on the box never reaches the
+ * `selectOnRowClick` of the row: a box is a control in a cell, and a control takes its own press.
+ */
+export function SelectRowCell<TRow>({
+  flat,
+  isActive,
+  selected,
+}: {
+  flat: FlatRow<TRow>;
+  isActive: boolean;
+  selected: boolean;
+}) {
+  const { labels, rowHeader, selection, textOf } = useGridContext<TRow>();
+  const text = rowHeader ? textOf(flat.row, rowHeader) : '';
+  return (
+    <td
+      className="flg-table-cell flg-data-grid-cell flg-data-grid-select-cell"
+      data-service="select"
+      tabIndex={-1}
+    >
+      <Checkbox
+        aria-label={labels.selectRow(text === '' ? String(flat.key) : text)}
+        checked={selected}
+        tabIndex={isActive ? 0 : -1}
+        onClick={(event) => selection.actions.press(flat.key, event.shiftKey)}
+      />
+    </td>
+  );
+}
+
+/**
+ * The box in the title of the column of boxes: it chooses, or takes off, the rows of its scope (the
+ * page, or every row), and is mixed when only some of them are chosen. With no row in its scope it is
+ * disabled and cannot have the focus, so the title cell takes the Tab stop for itself.
+ */
+export function SelectAllCell({ isActive }: { isActive: boolean }) {
+  const { labels, selection } = useGridContext();
+  const { header } = useContext(SelectionViewContext);
+  const name = selection.allMode === 'all' ? labels.selectAll : labels.selectAllOnPage;
+  return (
+    <th
+      scope="col"
+      className="flg-table-head flg-data-grid-head flg-data-grid-select-cell"
+      data-service="select"
+      tabIndex={isActive && header.disabled ? 0 : -1}
+    >
+      <Checkbox
+        aria-label={name}
+        checked={header.checked}
+        indeterminate={header.indeterminate}
+        disabled={header.disabled}
+        tabIndex={isActive && !header.disabled ? 0 : -1}
+        onCheckedChange={selection.actions.setAll}
+      />
+      {/* A title with no words is a table header with no name: the box has its own, and this says it
+          for the column. */}
+      <span className="flg-visually-hidden">{name}</span>
+    </th>
+  );
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,890 @@
+import { act, createEvent, fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
+import { StrictMode, createRef, useState } from 'react';
+import type { Ref } from 'react';
+import { renderToString } from 'react-dom/server';
+import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
+import { resetDevWarnings } from '../../internal/warn';
+import { DataGrid } from './DataGrid';
+import type { DataGridColumn, DataGridHandle, DataGridProps } from './index';
+
+// Virtual scrolling (spec phase 6 §3.7): only the rows near the viewport are in the DOM, two
+// spacers stand for the rest, and the row that has the keyboard is never dropped.
+
+const ROW = 41;
+const FRAME = 400;
+const HEAD = 41;
+
+const frames: Array<() => void> = [];
+
+beforeEach(() => {
+  resetDevWarnings();
+  HTMLElement.prototype.checkVisibility = () => true;
+  // The frame is 400px tall, a row is 41px and the heading is 41px; jsdom has no layout.
+  vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'clientHeight', 'get').mockImplementation(function (
+    this: HTMLElement,
+  ) {
+    return this.classList.contains('flg-table-frame') ? FRAME : 0;
+  });
+  vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'offsetHeight', 'get').mockImplementation(function (
+    this: HTMLElement,
+  ) {
+    return this.tagName === 'THEAD' ? HEAD : this.tagName === 'TR' ? ROW : 0;
+  });
+  // The frames are run by the test, so a scroll and the window that follows it are two steps.
+  vi.stubGlobal('requestAnimationFrame', (callback: FrameRequestCallback) => {
+    frames.push(() => callback(0));
+    return frames.length;
+  });
+  vi.stubGlobal('cancelAnimationFrame', (id: number) => {
+    frames[id - 1] = () => {};
+  });
+});
+afterEach(() => {
+  frames.length = 0;
+  vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+  vi.unstubAllEnvs();
+  Reflect.deleteProperty(HTMLElement.prototype, 'checkVisibility');
+  Reflect.deleteProperty(Element.prototype, 'scrollIntoView');
+  vi.restoreAllMocks();
+});
+
+interface Order {
+  id: string;
+  customer: string;
+  qty: number;
+}
+
+const makeOrders = (count: number): Order[] =>
+  Array.from({ length: count }, (_, index) => ({
+    id: `DH-${index + 1}`,
+    customer: `Customer ${index + 1}`,
+    qty: index + 1,
+  }));
+
+const ORDERS = makeOrders(200);
+const COLUMNS: DataGridColumn<Order>[] = [
+  { field: 'id', caption: 'Order', rowHeader: true, width: 104 },
+  { field: 'customer', caption: 'Customer', width: 200 },
+  { field: 'qty', caption: 'Qty', dataType: 'number', width: 80 },
+];
+
+function Orders({
+  gridRef,
+  ...props
+}: Partial<DataGridProps<Order>> & { gridRef?: Ref<DataGridHandle> }) {
+  return (
+    <DataGrid
+      ref={gridRef}
+      data={ORDERS}
+      rowKey="id"
+      columns={COLUMNS}
+      caption="Orders"
+      height={FRAME}
+      scrolling="virtual"
+      {...props}
+    />
+  );
+}
+
+const grid = () => screen.getByRole('grid');
+const frame = () => grid().parentElement as HTMLElement;
+const dataRows = () =>
+  Array.from(grid().querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('tbody > .flg-data-grid-row'));
+const spacers = () =>
+  Array.from(grid().querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('tbody > .flg-data-grid-spacer'));
+const rowIndexes = () => dataRows().map((row) => Number(row.getAttribute('aria-rowindex')));
+const heightOf = (spacer: HTMLElement) => (spacer.firstElementChild as HTMLElement).style.height;
+const cellOfRow = (rowindex: number, column = 1) =>
+  grid().querySelector<HTMLElement>(`tbody > [aria-rowindex="${rowindex}"]`)!.children[
+    column
+  ] as HTMLElement;
+const focusOn = (element: HTMLElement) => act(() => element.focus());
+const press = (element: HTMLElement, key: string, init: KeyboardEventInit = {}): boolean => {
+  const event = createEvent.keyDown(element, { key, bubbles: true, cancelable: true, ...init });
+  act(() => {
+    fireEvent(element, event);
+  });
+  return event.defaultPrevented;
+};
+/** Scrolls the frame, then lets the animation frame that applies it run. */
+const scrollTo = (top: number) => {
+  act(() => {
+    frame().scrollTop = top;
+    fireEvent.scroll(frame());
+  });
+  flushFrames();
+};
+const flushFrames = () => {
+  act(() => {
+    for (const run of frames.splice(0)) run();
+  });
+};
+
+describe('the window', () => {
+  it('draws the rows that are seen and 6 more on each side, and a spacer for the rest', () => {
+    render(<Orders />);
+    // 400px of 41px rows is rows 0 to 9; the row that begins at 410 is the first outside.
+    expect(rowIndexes()).toEqual(Array.from({ length: 16 }, (_, index) => index + 2));
+    expect(spacers()).toHaveLength(1);

+/** How many times a spy was called for a scroll listener on `target` (React has its own, on the root). */
+const scrollListeners = (
+  spy: { mock: { calls: unknown[][]; contexts: unknown[] } },
+  target: Element,
+): number =>
+  spy.mock.calls.filter(
+    (call, index) => call[0] === 'scroll' && spy.mock.contexts[index] === target,
+  ).length;
+
+describe('what runs only when it is on', () => {
+  it('listens to no scroll and observes nothing in a standard grid', () => {
+    const add = vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'addEventListener');
+    const observers: unknown[] = [];
+    vi.stubGlobal(
+      'ResizeObserver',
+      class {
+        constructor() {
+          observers.push(this);
+        }
+        observe() {}
+        unobserve() {}
+        disconnect() {}
+      },
+    );
+    render(<Orders scrolling="standard" paging={false} height={undefined} />);
+    expect(scrollListeners(add, frame())).toBe(0);
+    expect(observers).toHaveLength(0);
+    fireEvent.scroll(frame());
+    expect(frames).toHaveLength(0);
+  });
+
+  it('reads no row offset in a standard grid', () => {
+    const offsetTop = vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'offsetTop', 'get');
+    render(<Orders scrolling="standard" paging={false} />);
+    expect(offsetTop).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it('releases the listener, the frame and the observer on unmount', () => {
+    const remove = vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'removeEventListener');
+    const cancel = vi.fn();
+    vi.stubGlobal('cancelAnimationFrame', cancel);
+    const { unmount } = render(<Orders />);
+    const scrolled = frame();
+    act(() => {
+      fireEvent.scroll(scrolled);
+    });
+    unmount();
+    expect(scrollListeners(remove, scrolled)).toBe(1);
+    expect(cancel).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+    // A frame that was already asked for does nothing after that.
+    expect(() => flushFrames()).not.toThrow();
+  });
+
+  it('releases the listener when virtual goes off', () => {
+    const remove = vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'removeEventListener');
+    const add = vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'addEventListener');
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders paging={false} />);
+    const scrolled = frame();
+    expect(scrollListeners(add, scrolled)).toBe(1);
+    rerender(<Orders scrolling="standard" paging={false} />);
+    expect(scrollListeners(remove, scrolled)).toBe(1);
+  });
+});

+  beforeEach(() => {

+  it.each([['virtual'], ['standard']])(

+          columns={counted}

+## Virtual scrolling
+
+For a list too long to draw whole, pass `scrolling="virtual"` with a `height`. The grid then draws
+only the rows near what is seen, and an empty box above and below stands for the rest, so the DOM
+holds a few dozen rows however many there are, and the scroll bar is the one of the whole list. Ten
+thousand rows are a few dozen `<tr>`.
+
+<Canvas of={Stories.Virtual10000} />
+
+- **`height` is required**, and it is the prop: a grid that has its height from a stylesheet alone
+  scrolls as usual and warns once. The prop is also what the HTML from the server is made from: the
+  first window is the rows that `height` shows and 6 more when it is a number of pixels, and 20 rows
+  when it is a length (`'60vh'`).
+- **What is drawn:** the rows that meet the frame, 6 more on each side so that a quick scroll finds
+  rows there, and the row of the active cell, wherever the frame is scrolled. That row is never
+  taken out, so the focus does not fall to the page when you scroll away from it, and the grid does
+  not lose its one Tab stop. A spacer is a `tr` that is not a data row and is hidden from assistive
+  technology.
+- **Rows have a fixed height**, so the window is arithmetic: the distance between two rows is the
+  height of the table of the `density` and `variant`, measured on two neighbours once they are
+  drawn. A cell that is taller than its row is cut, as in any grid.
+- **`aria-rowcount` and `aria-rowindex`** are set in a virtual grid, and only there: the table
+  counts the heading and every row, and each drawn row says its place (the heading is row 1), so a
+  screen reader can say "row 5,000 of 10,001" for a row whose neighbours are not in the DOM. A grid
+  whose rows are all drawn does not set them.
+- **The keys go over every row:** <Kbd keys="mod+end" /> scrolls to the last row, draws it and
+  focuses it, and the arrows and <Kbd keys="pagedown" /> past what is drawn do the same for their
+  row.

+  (`paging={false}` is the same as leaving it out, and does not warn), and there is no bar.
+- **Not in server mode:** with `remote` the grid has a page and not the list, so it scrolls as usual
+  and warns once. Use the pages.
+- **Stripes** follow the place of a row in the list, so they do not move as rows come and go.
+
+### `scrollToRow`
+
+`ref.current.scrollToRow(key)` brings the row with that key into view, by the least it takes, and
+returns `true`. It returns `false` when no row has the key, and does nothing. In a grid with pages
+it goes to the page of the row first. It does not move the keyboard: the focus stays where it was.
+

+ * `<tr>` among its siblings is not its place in the list; `aria-rowindex` says it (1 for the heading,

+/** The `aria-rowindex` of the first row of data: the heading is the first row. */
+export const FIRST_ROW_INDEX = 2;

+/** The rows of data that are drawn, in order: the other rows of the body (the spacers) are not these. */
+export function dataRows(table: HTMLTableElement): HTMLTableRowElement[] {

+/** Scrolls the row at `index` of the list into view the least it takes, if it is drawn. */

+  // The frame's own scroll padding keeps it clear of the sticky heading. Not every DOM has the method.
+  if (row && typeof row.scrollIntoView === 'function') row.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' });
+}

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-virtual-rows.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-virtual-rows.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..fd239e2
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-virtual-rows.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,169 @@
+import { useCallback, useMemo, useState } from 'react';
+import type { RefObject } from 'react';
+import { useIsoLayoutEffect } from '../../../internal/use-iso-layout-effect';
+import { computeOffsets, findWindow, splitWindow } from '../engine/virtual';
+import type { WindowPart } from '../engine/virtual';
+import { dataRows, listIndexOf } from '../grid-dom';
+
+/** Rows drawn beyond the viewport on each side, so a fast scroll finds rows there before the next frame. */
+export const OVERSCAN = 6;
+
+interface Scroll {
+  /** The `scrollTop` of the frame. */
+  top: number;
+  /** The `clientHeight` of the frame; 0 until it is measured, and where there is no layout. */
+  viewport: number;
+}
+
+interface Measured {
+  /** The estimate this was measured under: a new estimate (density, variant, row height) drops it. */
+  estimate: number;
+  pitch: number;
+}
+
+export interface VirtualRowsOptions {
+  /** Whether the grid is virtual. When it is not, nothing is listened to, observed or measured. */
+  enabled: boolean;
+  frameRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>;
+  tableRef: RefObject<HTMLTableElement | null>;
+  /** How many rows there are in the list. */
+  count: number;
+  /** The height of a data row as the stylesheet draws it. */
+  rowHeight: number;
+  /** The distance between the tops of two rows before one is measured. */
+  estimate: number;
+  /** A row that is drawn although it is outside the window: the one that has the keyboard. */
+  keep: number | undefined;
+  /** A second row to keep for a while: the one the keyboard is leaving, until the focus has left it. */
+  hold: number | undefined;
+  /** How many rows the first window has, before the frame is measured (on the server too). */
+  firstRows: number;
+}
+
+export interface VirtualRows {
+  /** The window as parts to draw, in order; empty when the grid is not virtual. */
+  parts: readonly WindowPart[];
+  /** Scrolls the frame the least it takes for the row at `index` to be under the heading. */
+  scrollToIndex: (index: number) => void;
+}
+
+const NO_PARTS: readonly WindowPart[] = [];
+const NO_OFFSETS = new Float64Array(1);
+
+/**
+ * The window of a virtual list (spec phase 6 §3.7). The frame's scroll is read in a passive
+ * listener and applied once per animation frame, so a fast scroll makes one render per frame. The
+ * rows have a fixed height, so the offsets are sums of a pitch: the estimate the stylesheet's
+ * numbers give, and the distance of two neighbour rows once there are two in the DOM (measured
+ * with `offsetTop`, which a transform does not change). Until the frame has a height the window is
+ * the first `firstRows` rows, which is also what the server draws.
+ *
+ * A spacer is as tall as the rows it stands for, less the space a `striped` table puts between its
+ * rows: that is added around a row of its own, so left in, the rows would drift by 2px for each
+ * spacer.
+ */
+export function useVirtualRows({
+  enabled,
+  frameRef,
+  tableRef,
+  count,
+  rowHeight,
+  estimate,
+  keep,
+  hold,
+  firstRows,
+}: VirtualRowsOptions): VirtualRows {
+  const [scroll, setScroll] = useState<Scroll>({ top: 0, viewport: 0 });
+  const [measured, setMeasured] = useState<Measured | null>(null);
+  const pitch = measured?.estimate === estimate ? measured.pitch : estimate;
+
+  const offsets = useMemo(
+    () => (enabled ? computeOffsets(count, () => pitch) : NO_OFFSETS),
+    [enabled, count, pitch],
+  );
+
+  const parts = useMemo(() => {
+    if (!enabled) return NO_PARTS;
+    const window =
+      scroll.viewport > 0
+        ? findWindow(offsets, scroll.top, scroll.viewport, OVERSCAN)
+        : { start: 0, end: Math.min(count, firstRows) };
+    const gap = Math.max(0, estimate - rowHeight);
+    return splitWindow(offsets, window, [keep, hold]).map((part) =>
+      part.kind === 'spacer' ? { ...part, height: part.height - gap } : part,
+    );
+  }, [enabled, offsets, scroll, count, firstRows, estimate, rowHeight, keep, hold]);
+
+  // The scroll and the size of the frame.
+  useIsoLayoutEffect(() => {
+    const frame = frameRef.current;
+    if (!enabled || !frame) return undefined;
+    let pending = 0;
+    const read = (): void => {
+      pending = 0;
+      const next = { top: frame.scrollTop, viewport: frame.clientHeight };
+      setScroll((current) =>
+        current.top === next.top && current.viewport === next.viewport ? current : next,
+      );
+    };
+    const onScroll = (): void => {
+      if (pending === 0) pending = requestAnimationFrame(read);
+    };
+    frame.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll, { passive: true });
+    // The size is read now and when it changes; where nothing observes (jsdom) it is the one read.
+    read();
+    const observer =
+      typeof ResizeObserver === 'undefined' ? undefined : new ResizeObserver(() => read());
+    observer?.observe(frame);
+    return () => {
+      frame.removeEventListener('scroll', onScroll);
+      observer?.disconnect();
+      if (pending !== 0) cancelAnimationFrame(pending);
+    };
+  }, [enabled, frameRef]);
+
+  // The pitch: the distance of the tops of two rows that are neighbours in the list, as drawn.
+  const measurable = enabled && count > 1;
+  useIsoLayoutEffect(() => {
+    const table = tableRef.current;
+    if (!measurable || !table) return;
+    const rows = dataRows(table);
+    let distance = 0;
+    for (let at = 0; at + 1 < rows.length && distance === 0; at++) {
+      const first = rows[at]!;
+      const second = rows[at + 1]!;
+      if (listIndexOf(second, 0) - listIndexOf(first, 0) === 1) {
+        distance = second.offsetTop - first.offsetTop;
+      }
+    }
+    setMeasured((current) => {
+      if (distance <= 0) return current?.estimate === estimate ? current : null;
+      return current?.estimate === estimate && current.pitch === distance
+        ? current
+        : { estimate, pitch: distance };
+    });
+  }, [measurable, estimate, tableRef]);
+
+  const scrollToIndex = useCallback(
+    (index: number): void => {
+      const frame = frameRef.current;
+      if (!enabled || !frame || !(index >= 0 && index < count)) return;
+      // The heading is stuck over the first `head` pixels of the frame, so a row at `top` in the
+      // list is `head + top` into what scrolls.
+      const head = tableRef.current?.tHead?.offsetHeight ?? 0;
+      const top = offsets[index]!;
+      const bottom = offsets[index + 1]!;
+      let next = frame.scrollTop;
+      if (top < next) next = top;
+      else if (bottom + head > next + frame.clientHeight) next = bottom + head - frame.clientHeight;
+      if (next === frame.scrollTop) return;
+      frame.scrollTop = next;
+      // The window is made now and not at the next scroll event, so a row that is not drawn is
+      // there for the focus that follows.
+      setScroll({ top: next, viewport: frame.clientHeight });
+    },
+    [enabled, frameRef, tableRef, offsets, count],
+  );
+
+  return { parts, scrollToIndex };
+}

+import { act, fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
+import { StrictMode, createRef } from 'react';
+import { renderToString } from 'react-dom/server';
+import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
+import type { Mock } from 'vitest';
+import { resetDevWarnings } from '../../internal/warn';
+import { DataGrid } from './DataGrid';
+import { LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY } from './hooks/use-loading-announce';
+import { skeletonWidth } from './parts/SkeletonRows';
+import type { DataGridColumn, DataGridHandle, DataGridProps } from './index';
+
+beforeEach(() => {
+  resetDevWarnings();
+  vi.restoreAllMocks();
+});
+afterEach(() => {
+  vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+  vi.restoreAllMocks();
+});
+
+interface Order {
+  id: string;
+  customer: string;
+  qty: number;
+  total: number;
+}
+
+const ORDERS: Order[] = [
+  { id: 'DH-1030', customer: 'Nguyễn Minh', qty: 4, total: 1250000 },
+  { id: 'DH-1029', customer: 'Trần Hải', qty: 1, total: 890000 },
+  { id: 'DH-1028', customer: 'Lê An', qty: 12, total: 15400000 },
+];
+
+const COLUMNS: DataGridColumn<Order>[] = [
+  { field: 'id', caption: 'Order', rowHeader: true, width: 104 },
+  { field: 'customer', caption: 'Customer', width: 200 },
+  { field: 'qty', caption: 'Qty', dataType: 'number', width: 80 },
+  { field: 'total', caption: 'Total', dataType: 'number', width: 160 },
+];
+
+function Orders(props: Partial<DataGridProps<Order>>) {
+  return <DataGrid data={ORDERS} rowKey="id" columns={COLUMNS} caption="Orders" {...props} />;
+}
+
+const grid = () => screen.getByRole('grid') as HTMLTableElement;
+const root = () => grid().closest('.flg-data-grid') as HTMLElement;
+const main = () => root().querySelector('.flg-data-grid-main') as HTMLElement;
+const frame = () => grid().parentElement as HTMLElement;
+const skeletonRows = () =>
+  Array.from(grid().querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('tbody > tr.flg-data-grid-skeleton-row'));
+const dataRows = () =>
+  Array.from(grid().querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('tbody > tr.flg-data-grid-row'));
+const overlay = () => root().querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-overlay');
+const emptyRows = () => Array.from(grid().querySelectorAll('tbody > tr.flg-data-grid-empty'));
+const said = () => (root().lastElementChild as HTMLElement).textContent;
+
+describe('the first load: no rows and loading', () => {
+  it.each([
+    [undefined, 20],
+    [{ pageSize: 12 }, 12],
+    [{ pageSize: 50, pageSizes: [50] }, 20],
+    [{ pageSize: 4 }, 4],
+    [false, 20],
+  ] as const)(
+    'draws as many skeleton rows as a page holds, and no more than 20: %j gives %i',
+    (paging, count) => {
+      render(<Orders data={[]} loading paging={paging} />);
+      expect(skeletonRows()).toHaveLength(count);
+    },
+  );
+
+  it('follows the size of the page that is asked for, and is 20 when the grid has no pages', () => {
+    const { unmount } = render(<Orders data={[]} loading defaultPage={{ index: 0, size: 7 }} />);
+    expect(skeletonRows()).toHaveLength(7);
+    unmount();
+    render(<Orders data={[]} loading paging={false} defaultPage={{ index: 0, size: 7 }} />);
+    expect(skeletonRows()).toHaveLength(20);
+  });
+
+  it('draws a cell for each column, and in each a text skeleton whose width is fixed by its column', () => {
+    render(<Orders data={[]} loading paging={{ pageSize: 3 }} />);
+    const rows = skeletonRows();
+    expect(rows).toHaveLength(3);
+    for (const row of rows) {
+      expect(row.children).toHaveLength(COLUMNS.length);
+      const blocks = Array.from(row.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.flg-skeleton'));
+      expect(blocks).toHaveLength(COLUMNS.length);
+      expect(blocks.map((block) => block.style.width)).toEqual(['40%', '57%', '74%', '50%']);
+      for (const block of blocks) {
+        expect(block).toHaveAttribute('data-shape', 'text');
+        expect(block).toHaveAttribute('data-variant', 'pulse');
+      }
+    }
+  });
+
+  it('keeps the width of a column the same when the column of boxes is added in front of it', () => {
+    render(<Orders data={[]} loading selectionMode="multiple" paging={{ pageSize: 2 }} />);
+    const row = skeletonRows()[0] as HTMLElement;
+    // The column of boxes has nothing in it; the others count from the first column of the caller's.
+    expect(row.children).toHaveLength(COLUMNS.length + 1);
+    expect(row.children[0]?.querySelector('.flg-skeleton')).toBeNull();
+    const widths = Array.from(row.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.flg-skeleton')).map(
+      (block) => block.style.width,
+    );
+    expect(widths).toEqual(['40%', '57%', '74%', '50%']);
+  });
+
+  it('is always between 40% and 80%, and only a function of the index of the column', () => {
+    for (let index = 0; index < 200; index++) {
+      const width = skeletonWidth(index);
+      expect(width).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(40);
+      expect(width).toBeLessThanOrEqual(80);
+      expect(Number.isInteger(width)).toBe(true);
+    }
+    expect(skeletonWidth(0)).toBe(40);
+    expect(skeletonWidth(3)).toBe(50);
+  });
+
+  it('is the same on every render and on the server: nothing random', () => {
+    const random = vi.spyOn(Math, 'random');
+    const first = render(<Orders data={[]} loading paging={{ pageSize: 5 }} />);
+    const body = () => grid().querySelector('tbody')?.innerHTML;
+    const before = body();
+    first.rerender(<Orders data={[]} loading paging={{ pageSize: 5 }} />);
+    expect(body()).toBe(before);
+    first.unmount();
+    render(<Orders data={[]} loading paging={{ pageSize: 5 }} />);
+    expect(body()).toBe(before);
+    // The server writes the same rows each time, with the widths the client draws (the two spell a
+    // `style` differently, so the widths are read out of it).
+    const html = () => renderToString(<Orders data={[]} loading paging={{ pageSize: 5 }} />);
+    const server = html();
+    expect(html()).toBe(server);
+    const widths = (markup: string) => Array.from(markup.matchAll(/width: ?(\d+)%/g), (m) => m[1]);
+    expect(widths(server)).toHaveLength(5 * COLUMNS.length);
+    expect(widths(server)).toEqual(widths(before ?? ''));
+    expect(random).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it('hides the rows from what reads the page, and they are not rows of data', () => {
+    render(<Orders data={[]} loading selectionMode="multiple" />);
+    const rows = skeletonRows();
+    expect(rows.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+    for (const row of rows) {
+      expect(row).toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
+      expect(row).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-selected');
+      expect(row).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-rowindex');
+    }
+    expect(dataRows()).toHaveLength(0);
+    // Nothing in them can be reached by the keyboard, and the grid's one stop is the heading.
+    expect(grid().querySelectorAll('tbody [tabindex], tbody input, tbody button')).toHaveLength(0);
+    const stops = grid().querySelectorAll('[tabindex="0"]');
+    expect(stops).toHaveLength(1);
+    expect(stops[0]?.closest('thead')).not.toBeNull();
+  });
+
+  it('has no pager and no empty row while it waits', () => {
+    render(<Orders data={[]} loading />);
+    expect(root().querySelector('.flg-data-grid-pager')).toBeNull();
+    expect(emptyRows()).toHaveLength(0);
+    expect(overlay()).toBeNull();
+  });
+
+  it('gives way to the rows when they arrive, and comes back when the rows go, on a mounted grid', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders data={[]} loading />);
+    expect(skeletonRows().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+    rerender(<Orders data={ORDERS} />);
+    expect(skeletonRows()).toHaveLength(0);
+    expect(dataRows()).toHaveLength(3);
+    rerender(<Orders data={[]} loading />);
+    expect(dataRows()).toHaveLength(0);
+    expect(skeletonRows().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+  });
+
+  it('draws a stripe on the skeleton rows of a striped grid as on its rows, by the odd child', () => {
+    render(<Orders data={[]} loading variant="striped" paging={{ pageSize: 3 }} />);
+    // They are rows of Table's own classes, so Table's stripe is on the odd children.
+    for (const row of skeletonRows()) expect(row).toHaveClass('flg-table-row');
+  });
+});
+
+describe('loading with rows: the overlay', () => {
+  it('has no overlay while the grid is not loading, and one over the rows when it is', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders />);
+    expect(overlay()).toBeNull();
+    rerender(<Orders loading />);
+    const layer = overlay() as HTMLElement;
+    expect(layer).not.toBeNull();
+    expect(layer).toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
+    // The old rows stay; there are no skeleton rows.
+    expect(dataRows()).toHaveLength(3);
+    expect(skeletonRows()).toHaveLength(0);
+    rerender(<Orders />);
+    expect(overlay()).toBeNull();
+  });
+
+  it('sits in the main part, after the frame, so it does not scroll with the rows', () => {
+    render(<Orders loading />);

+
+  it('covers neither the caption nor the bar of the pages: it is not in them', () => {

+      expect(main().contains(part)).toBe(false);

+
+  it("holds a Spinner that says the loading label, and the label is the caller's to give", () => {

+
+  it('is the overlay in a server grid too, the same as on the client', () => {

+  });
+
+  it('is loading in server mode too: the page that is shown stays under it', () => {
+    render(<Orders remote totalCount={90} loading />);
+    expect(overlay()).not.toBeNull();
+    expect(dataRows()).toHaveLength(3);
+  });
+
+  const place = (element: Element, property: string, value: number) =>
+    Object.defineProperty(element, property, { configurable: true, value });
+
+  // Sizes as an engine reports them: the stylesheet of the library is not loaded in these tests.
+  const sizes = (head: number, body: number) => {
+    place(grid().tHead as HTMLElement, 'offsetHeight', head);
+    place(grid().tBodies[0] as HTMLElement, 'offsetTop', body);
+  };
+
+  it('is below the heading: its top is the bottom of the measured heading', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders />);
+    // A lined table has no spacing: the body starts where the heading ends.
+    sizes(33, 33);
+    rerender(<Orders loading />);
+    expect(overlay()?.style.top).toBe('33px');
+  });
+
+  it('adds what is above the table in the frame', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders />);
+    // A `striped` frame is pulled up by its margin over its padding (the table starts 6px down in it); a
+    // `lined` one has its edge.
+    place(frame(), 'offsetTop', -6);
+    place(frame(), 'clientTop', 1);
+    place(grid(), 'offsetTop', 6);
+    sizes(31, 31);
+    rerender(<Orders loading />);
+    expect(overlay()?.style.top).toBe(`${-6 + 1 + 6 + 31}px`);
+  });
+
+  it('counts the spacing above the heading where the engine draws it, and not where it does not', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders />);
+    // 2px of spacing above the heading and 2px under it: the heading ends 2px after its own height.
+    sizes(26, 30);
+    rerender(<Orders loading />);
+    expect(overlay()?.style.top).toBe('28px');
+    rerender(<Orders />);
+    // The same table in an engine that draws none: the body starts where the heading ends.
+    sizes(26, 26);
+    rerender(<Orders loading />);
+    expect(overlay()?.style.top).toBe('26px');
+  });
+
+  it('leaves the top to the stylesheet where the heading has no size to measure', () => {
+    render(<Orders loading />);
+    expect(overlay()?.style.top).toBe('');
+  });
+
+  it('follows the heading when it changes size, and is measured only while it is there', () => {
+    const observers: { callback: ResizeObserverCallback; disconnect: () => void }[] = [];
+    class FakeObserver {
+      constructor(callback: ResizeObserverCallback) {
+        observers.push({ callback, disconnect: vi.fn() });
+        this.index = observers.length - 1;
+      }
+      private readonly index: number;
+      observe() {}
+      unobserve() {}
+      disconnect() {
+        observers[this.index]?.disconnect();
+      }
+    }
+    vi.stubGlobal('ResizeObserver', FakeObserver);
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders />);
+    // Nothing is watched for a grid that does not load, with a width on every column and no height.
+    expect(observers).toHaveLength(0);
+    const head = vi.spyOn(grid().tHead as HTMLElement, 'offsetHeight', 'get').mockReturnValue(33);
+    const body = vi.spyOn(grid().tBodies[0] as HTMLElement, 'offsetTop', 'get').mockReturnValue(33);
+    rerender(<Orders loading />);
+    expect(observers).toHaveLength(1);
+    expect(overlay()?.style.top).toBe('33px');
+    head.mockReturnValue(41);
+    body.mockReturnValue(41);
+    act(() => observers[0]?.callback([], {} as ResizeObserver));
+    expect(overlay()?.style.top).toBe('41px');
+    rerender(<Orders />);
+    expect(observers[0]?.disconnect).toHaveBeenCalled();
+    expect(overlay()).toBeNull();
+  });
+
+  it('takes the data rows into no account: they keep their keys, their roles and their keyboard', () => {
+    render(<Orders loading selectionMode="single" />);
+    expect(dataRows()).toHaveLength(3);
+    expect(dataRows()[0]).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'false');
+    const stops = grid().querySelectorAll('[tabindex="0"]');
+    expect(stops).toHaveLength(1);
+    expect(stops[0]?.closest('tbody')).not.toBeNull();
+  });
+});
+
+describe('aria-busy', () => {
+  it('is on the table while the grid loads, with rows or without, and not before or after', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders />);
+    expect(grid()).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-busy');
+    rerender(<Orders loading />);
+    expect(grid()).toHaveAttribute('aria-busy', 'true');
+    rerender(<Orders />);
+    expect(grid()).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-busy');
+    rerender(<Orders data={[]} loading />);
+    expect(grid()).toHaveAttribute('aria-busy', 'true');
+    rerender(<Orders data={[]} />);
+    expect(grid()).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-busy');
+  });
+
+  it('is only a true loading: a value that is not a boolean is not loading', () => {
+    // @ts-expect-error a string is not a `loading`

+  it('leaves the aria attributes of the caller on the table', () => {

+    expect(grid()).toHaveAttribute('aria-busy', 'true');

+});
+
+describe('announcing the loading', () => {
+  beforeEach(() => {
+    vi.useFakeTimers();
+  });
+  afterEach(() => {
+    vi.useRealTimers();
+  });
+  // Async, so that what a MutationObserver saw is delivered before the next step.
+  const wait = (ms: number) =>
+    act(async () => {
+      vi.advanceTimersByTime(ms);
+    });
+
+  // Every text the region takes, in order, so that a sentence said twice is seen twice.
+  function recordRegion(): string[] {
+    const texts: string[] = [];
+    const observer = new MutationObserver(() => {
+      const text = said();
+      if (text) texts.push(text);
+    });
+    observer.observe(root().lastElementChild as HTMLElement, {
+      childList: true,
+      characterData: true,
+      subtree: true,
+    });
+    return texts;
+  }
+
+  it('says nothing for a grid that is not loading', async () => {
+    render(<Orders />);
+    await wait(LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY * 3);
+    expect(said()).toBe('');
+  });
+
+  it('says the label once, when loading starts', async () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders />);
+    const texts = recordRegion();
+    rerender(<Orders loading />);
+    await wait(LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY - 1);
+    expect(said()).toBe('');
+    await wait(2);
+    expect(said()).toBe('Loading…');
+    // Still loading, and the grid draws again: it does not say it again.
+    rerender(<Orders loading caption="Orders" />);
+    await wait(LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY * 3);
+    expect(texts).toEqual(['Loading…']);
+  });
+
+  it('says it for a grid that mounts loading, with rows or without', async () => {
+    const { unmount } = render(<Orders data={[]} loading />);
+    await wait(LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY + 1);
+    expect(said()).toBe('Loading…');
+    unmount();
+    render(<Orders loading />);
+    await wait(LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY + 1);
+    expect(said()).toBe('Loading…');
+  });
+
+  it('says it once when the loading flips and flips back quickly', async () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders />);
+    const texts = recordRegion();
+    rerender(<Orders loading />);
+    await wait(100);
+    rerender(<Orders />);
+    await wait(50);
+    rerender(<Orders loading />);
+    await wait(LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY * 4);
+    expect(said()).toBe('Loading…');
+    expect(texts).toEqual(['Loading…']);
+  });
+
+  it('says nothing for a load of half a second, and says it once for one of 1.2 s', async () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders />);
+    const texts = recordRegion();
+    rerender(<Orders loading />);
+    await wait(500);
+    rerender(<Orders />);
+    await wait(LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY * 3);
+    expect(said()).toBe('');
+    expect(texts).toEqual([]);
+    rerender(<Orders loading />);
+    await wait(1200);
+    expect(said()).toBe('Loading…');
+    rerender(<Orders />);
+    await wait(LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY * 3);
+    expect(texts).toEqual(['Loading…']);
+  });
+
+  it('waits a full second', async () => {
+    expect(LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY).toBe(1000);
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders />);
+    rerender(<Orders loading />);
+    await wait(999);
+    expect(said()).toBe('');
+    await wait(2);
+    expect(said()).toBe('Loading…');
+  });
+
+  it('keeps the sentence of a sort that the same press started a load with', async () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders remote totalCount={3} />);
+    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /Qty/ }));
+    // The app answers the press by loading.
+    rerender(<Orders remote totalCount={3} loading />);
+    await wait(50);
+    expect(said()).toBe('Sorted by Qty, ascending');
+    await wait(LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY + 100);
+    // Only when the load has gone on for a second does the grid say that it is loading.
+    expect(said()).toBe('Loading…');
+  });
+
+  it('says it again for the next load, which is a new one', async () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders />);
+    const texts = recordRegion();
+    rerender(<Orders loading />);
+    await wait(LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY + 1);
+    rerender(<Orders />);
+    await wait(10);
+    rerender(<Orders loading />);
+    // The region is emptied a task before it has the words again, so the same sentence is read again.
+    await wait(LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY);
+    await wait(1);
+    expect(texts).toEqual(['Loading…', 'Loading…']);
+  });
+
+  it('says the label the caller gives, and not a change of the label as a new loading', async () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders loading labels={{ loading: 'Đang tải' }} />);
+    const texts = recordRegion();
+    await wait(LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY + 1);
+    expect(said()).toBe('Đang tải');
+    rerender(<Orders loading labels={{ loading: 'Chờ chút' }} />);
+    await wait(LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY * 3);
+    expect(texts).toEqual(['Đang tải']);
+  });
+
+  it('says it once in StrictMode, which runs the effects twice', async () => {
+    render(
+      <StrictMode>
+        <Orders loading />
+      </StrictMode>,
+    );
+    const texts = recordRegion();
+    await wait(LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY * 3);
+    expect(said()).toBe('Loading…');
+    expect(texts).toEqual(['Loading…']);
+  });
+
+  it('leaves no wait behind when the grid is gone before it is said', () => {
+    const { unmount } = render(<Orders loading />);
+    expect(vi.getTimerCount()).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+    unmount();
+    expect(vi.getTimerCount()).toBe(0);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('empty: no rows and not loading', () => {

+  it("spans the column of boxes too, and says the caller's words", () => {

+    expect(root().querySelector('.flg-data-grid-pager')).not.toBeNull();

+
+  it('is what a grid of server mode with no rows shows', () => {

+  it('is replaced by the skeleton when it loads, and is not busy when it is empty', () => {

+    expect(grid()).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-busy');
+    rerender(<Orders data={[]} loading />);

+    expect(skeletonRows()).toHaveLength(0);
+  });
+
+  it('is the same on the server', () => {

+    expect(row).toHaveTextContent('No data');
+    expect(container.querySelectorAll('tbody > tr')).toHaveLength(1);

+});
+
+describe('the width of what spans every column', () => {
+  interface Watcher {
+    callback: ResizeObserverCallback;
+    targets: Element[];
+    disconnect: Mock<() => void>;
+  }
+  function stubObserver(): Watcher[] {
+    const watchers: Watcher[] = [];
+    class FakeObserver {
+      private readonly watcher: Watcher;
+      constructor(callback: ResizeObserverCallback) {
+        this.watcher = { callback, targets: [], disconnect: vi.fn() };
+        watchers.push(this.watcher);
+      }
+      observe(target: Element) {
+        this.watcher.targets.push(target);
+      }
+      unobserve() {}
+      disconnect() {
+        this.watcher.disconnect();
+      }
+    }
+    vi.stubGlobal('ResizeObserver', FakeObserver);
+    return watchers;
+  }
+  const FRAME_WIDTH = '--flg-data-grid-frame-width';
+
+  it('is measured while the empty row is shown, even when every column has a width', () => {
+    const watchers = stubObserver();

+    render(<Orders data={[]} />);
+    expect(watchers).toHaveLength(1);
+    expect(watchers[0]?.targets).toEqual([frame()]);
+    expect(frame().style.getPropertyValue(FRAME_WIDTH)).toBe('640px');
+    // The columns keep the widths they have: only a flexible column is spread over the room.
+    expect(Array.from(grid().querySelectorAll('col')).map((col) => col.style.width)).toEqual(
+      COLUMNS.map((column) => `${column.width}px`),
+    );
+  });
+
+  it('follows the frame while it is empty, and lets go when rows come', () => {
+    const watchers = stubObserver();
+    const clientWidth = vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'clientWidth', 'get').mockReturnValue(640);
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders data={[]} />);
+    clientWidth.mockReturnValue(500);
+    act(() => watchers[0]?.callback([], {} as ResizeObserver));
+    expect(frame().style.getPropertyValue(FRAME_WIDTH)).toBe('500px');
+    rerender(<Orders />);
+    expect(watchers[0]?.disconnect).toHaveBeenCalled();
+    expect(frame().style.getPropertyValue(FRAME_WIDTH)).toBe('');
+  });
+
+  it('measures nothing for a grid with rows and a width on every column', () => {
+    const watchers = stubObserver();
+    render(<Orders />);
+    expect(watchers).toHaveLength(0);
+  });
+
+  it('measures nothing for the skeleton: it is as wide as the columns are', () => {
+    const watchers = stubObserver();
+    render(<Orders data={[]} loading />);
+    expect(watchers).toHaveLength(0);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('the handle', () => {
+  it('has exactly the four members the grid has so far', () => {

+    const ref = createRef<DataGridHandle>();

+// Loading and empty are outside the mockups (spec phase 6 §4.3): drawn in G1's frame with the values the
+// spec gives. Each story says `loading` itself (an arg of the render, no timer), so the shot is the same
+// whenever it is taken. The skeleton pulses without end: GridLoading is shot a second time with the
+// motion stopped, as Skeleton's own stories are. The spinner of GridReloading turns without end too,
+// and like Spinner's stories it is shot as the harness leaves a running animation, at its start (the
+// pass for `reduced-motion` shows what a person who asked for less motion sees, and the spinner still
+// turns then, only slower, so it has no pass of its own).
+
+/** The first load: the heading of GridCore over a page of 12 skeleton rows of the height of a row. */
+export const GridLoading: Story = {
+  tags: ['viewport-1440x720', 'reduced-motion'],
+  render: () => (
+    <SalesGrid
+      variant="lined"
+      data={[]}
+      loading
+      defaultSelectedKeys={[]}
+      description="Loading orders · Lumen, November 2026"
+    />
+  ),
+  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
+    const table = canvasElement.querySelector('table')!;
+    const rows = Array.from(table.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('tbody > tr'));
+    await expect(rows).toHaveLength(12);
+    await expect(table).toHaveAttribute('aria-busy', 'true');
+    // A row of skeleton is as tall as a row of data: the 41px of the table of spec 4.3 (lined, md).
+    for (const row of rows) {
+      await expect(row.offsetHeight).toBe(rowPitch(ROW_HEIGHT.standard.lined, 'lined'));
+      await expect(row.getAttribute('aria-hidden')).toBe('true');
+    }
+    await expect(canvasElement.querySelector('.flg-data-grid-pager')).toBeNull();
+  },
+};
+
+/** Loading again: GridCore as it is, under a wash with a spinner from the bottom of the heading. */
+export const GridReloading: Story = {
+  tags: ['viewport-1440x720'],
+  render: () => <SalesGrid variant="lined" height={459} loading />,
+  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
+    const table = canvasElement.querySelector('table')!;
+    const layer = canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-overlay')!;
+    await expect(table).toHaveAttribute('aria-busy', 'true');
+    await expect(table.querySelectorAll('tbody > tr.flg-data-grid-row')).toHaveLength(12);
+    // It starts where the heading ends, and ends with the frame.
+    const frame = table.parentElement as HTMLElement;
+    const head = table.tHead!.getBoundingClientRect();
+    await expect(Math.abs(layer.getBoundingClientRect().top - head.bottom)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);
+    await expect(
+      Math.abs(layer.getBoundingClientRect().bottom - frame.getBoundingClientRect().bottom),
+    ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);
+  },
+};
+
+/** No rows and not loading: one cell across the nine columns, with the words. */
+export const GridEmpty: Story = {
+  tags: ['viewport-1440x720'],
+  render: () => (
+    <SalesGrid
+      variant="lined"
+      data={[]}
+      defaultSelectedKeys={[]}
+      description="0 orders · Lumen, November 2026"
+    />

+## Loading and empty
+
+`loading` says that the data is on its way. It is the same on the server and in the browser, and
+what it shows depends on whether there is anything to show:
+
+- **Nothing yet** (`loading` and no row): a page of skeleton rows stands where the rows will be: as
+  many as a page holds (`paging.pageSize`, or the page size in use), and at most 20; 20 when the grid
+  has no pages. They are as tall as rows of data, and are ruled or striped as the rows of the grid
+  are, since they are rows of a Table. Each cell of a column holds a `Skeleton` that pulses, as wide as 40% to 80%
+  of the cell, fixed by the place of the column, so no two renders differ and the blocks do not line
+  up. The column of boxes of `selectionMode="multiple"` has none. The rows are hidden from assistive
+  technology, are not rows of data (no `aria-selected`) and cannot have the keyboard; the heading is
+  the one stop of Tab, and there is no bar of pages.
+- **Rows already** (`loading` and rows, which is a load that replaces what is shown, a new page in
+  server mode, say): the rows stay, and a layer goes over them, from the bottom of the heading to the
+  bottom of the frame, with a `Spinner` in the middle of what is seen. It is a wash of the surface,
+  `color-mix(in srgb, var(--flg-glass-tint-solid) 55%, transparent)`, and in forced colours it is
+  transparent and the spinner shows. The layer is only to look at and takes no pointer: the wheel, the scrollbar and a press reach the
+  frame and the cells under it, and the heading, the caption and the bar of the pages stay in use. It is in the main part of the grid, not in
+  the frame, so it does not scroll with the rows. The keyboard still works, so a load that is slow does
+  not trap anyone; it is for the app to ignore what it does not want while it loads. The grid measures
+  its heading to place the layer, only while the layer is there.
+- **Either way** the table is `aria-busy="true"`, and the grid says `labels.loading` once, when the
+  load has lasted a second, through its live region: `aria-busy` already says that it is loading, and
+  a load that is over sooner is not worth a sentence. A `loading` that goes off and on again within
+  that second is one load, and the next load says it again. Nothing is said to the region before
+  then and nothing is cleared from it, so a sort that you announce in the same press is heard.
+
+<Canvas of={Stories.LoadingStates} />
+
+An empty grid (no row and not `loading`) draws one row with one cell across every column, and in it
+`labels.noData` ("No data"): centred, wrapping, in the small semibold text, with padding of 26px at
+the top and the bottom. It is not a row of data and nothing in it takes the keyboard, so the active
+cell is a title, and there is no bar of pages. The words are as wide as what the frame shows and stay
+at its left edge when the columns are wider than the frame and it has been scrolled sideways, so the
+grid measures its frame while they are drawn.
+
+<Canvas of={Stories.EmptyScrolled} />
+
+What an empty grid draws is only the words, which are yours through `labels.noData`: there is no icon,
+no button and no other message yet.
+

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-loading-announce.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-loading-announce.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..48c9340
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-loading-announce.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,33 @@
+import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
+import type { UseAnnounceResult } from '../../../internal/use-announce';
+import { useWriteOnCommit } from '../../../internal/use-write-on-commit';
+
+/**
+ * How long a load has to last before it is said, in milliseconds. `aria-busy` already says that the
+ * table is loading; the sentence is for a load that goes on, and a shorter one is not worth it.
+ */
+export const LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY = 1000;
+
+/**
+ * Says `text` once when `loading` has lasted `LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY`. The wait is a timer of its own,
+ * started when `loading` turns on and cleared when it turns off or the grid goes, so a load that
+ * flips off and on says it once and a short one says nothing. Nothing is said to the region before
+ * then, and nothing is cleared from it: a sentence that was said in the same press (a sort) is
+ * heard, and not replaced. The words are read when they are said and are not a reason to say them
+ * again.
+ */
+export function useLoadingAnnounce(
+  loading: boolean,
+  text: string,
+  announce: UseAnnounceResult['announce'],
+): void {
+  const words = useRef(text);
+  useWriteOnCommit(() => {
+    words.current = text;
+  });
+  useEffect(() => {
+    if (!loading) return undefined;
+    const timer = setTimeout(() => announce(words.current), LOADING_ANNOUNCE_DELAY);
+    return () => clearTimeout(timer);
+  }, [loading, announce]);
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-overlay-top.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-overlay-top.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..bc44350
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-overlay-top.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,55 @@
+import { useState } from 'react';
+import type { RefObject } from 'react';
+import { useIsoLayoutEffect } from '../../../internal/use-iso-layout-effect';
+
+/**
+ * Where the layer over a grid that loads starts: the bottom of the heading, in pixels from the top of
+ * the main part that the layer is positioned in. It is measured, from layout sizes (`offsetTop`,
+ * `offsetHeight`, `clientTop`, which a transform does not change), because the frame is not always at
+ * the top of the main part and the heading not always at the top of the frame: a `striped` or
+ * `minimal` frame is pulled up by its margin over its own padding, a `lined` one has an edge, and a
+ * `striped` table has spacing of 2px around every row group, above the heading and between it and the
+ * body, where an engine draws it (WebKit draws none there).
+ *
+ * The heading is `position: sticky`, so its own `offsetTop` says where it is stuck and not where it
+ * rests. The body is not sticky: it starts after the heading and the spacing under it, and the
+ * spacing above the heading is the same, so the bottom of the heading, at rest, is half way between
+ * the top of the body and the heading's own height. That holds whether the engine draws the spacing
+ * (the two are then 2px apart each side) or not (the body starts where the heading ends), and the
+ * stylesheet's value is not read. Nothing is measured unless `active`; `undefined` until the table
+ * has a body with a place, and where there is none to measure (a server, jsdom) the stylesheet's
+ * estimate stands.
+ */
+export function useOverlayTop(
+  frameRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>,
+  tableRef: RefObject<HTMLTableElement | null>,
+  active: boolean,
+): number | undefined {
+  const [top, setTop] = useState<number | undefined>(undefined);
+
+  useIsoLayoutEffect(() => {
+    const frame = frameRef.current;
+    const table = tableRef.current;
+    if (!active || !frame || !table) return undefined;
+    const measure = () => {
+      const body = table.tBodies[0];
+      const headHeight = table.tHead?.offsetHeight ?? 0;
+      if (!body || body.offsetTop === 0 || headHeight === 0) {
+        setTop(undefined);
+        return;
+      }
+      setTop(
+        frame.offsetTop + frame.clientTop + table.offsetTop + (body.offsetTop + headHeight) / 2,
+      );
+    };
+    measure();
+    if (typeof ResizeObserver === 'undefined') return undefined;
+    // The heading changes size with what is in it, and the table with the heading.
+    const observer = new ResizeObserver(measure);
+    observer.observe(table);
+    if (table.tHead) observer.observe(table.tHead);
+    return () => observer.disconnect();
+  }, [frameRef, tableRef, active]);
+
+  return active ? top : undefined;
+}

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/parts/EmptyRow.tsx b/src/components/data-grid/parts/EmptyRow.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..9705363
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/parts/EmptyRow.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,19 @@
+import { useGridContext } from '../grid-context';
+
+/**
+ * What a grid with no row says: one row with one cell across every column, and the words in it. The
+ * words are in a box that sticks to the left edge of the frame and is as wide as what the frame
+ * shows (`--flg-data-grid-frame-width`, which the grid measures while this is drawn), so they stay
+ * in sight when the columns are wider than the frame and it has been scrolled sideways. It is not a
+ * row of data and nothing in it takes the keyboard.
+ */
+export function EmptyRow() {
+  const { columns, labels } = useGridContext();
+  return (
+    <tr className="flg-data-grid-empty">
+      <td className="flg-data-grid-empty-cell" colSpan={columns.length}>
+        <div className="flg-data-grid-empty-content">{labels.noData}</div>
+      </td>
+    </tr>
+  );
+}

+interface OverlayProps {
+  variant: TableVariant;
+  /** The words of the spinner, which no one hears: the layer is hidden, and the grid says it itself. */
+  label: string;
+  /** Where the layer starts, in pixels, once the heading is measured. */
+  top: number | undefined;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The layer over the rows of a grid that loads again, from the bottom of the heading to the bottom of
+ * the frame, with a spinner in the middle of what is seen. It is decorative: `aria-hidden`, and the
+ * state is said by `aria-busy` and the live region. It is in the main part and not in the frame, so
+ * it stays put when the rows scroll; it takes no pointer (`pointer-events: none`), so what is under it
+ * is reached, and it does not reach the heading, the caption or the bar of the pages.
+ */
+export function Overlay({ variant, label, top }: OverlayProps) {
+  const style: CSSProperties | undefined = top === undefined ? undefined : { top };
+  return (
+    <div className="flg-data-grid-overlay" data-variant={variant} aria-hidden="true" style={style}>
+      <Spinner size="md" label={label} />
+    </div>
+  );
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/parts/SkeletonRows.tsx b/src/components/data-grid/parts/SkeletonRows.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..d61bfa7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/parts/SkeletonRows.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+import { Skeleton } from '../../skeleton/Skeleton';
+import { useGridContext } from '../grid-context';
+
+/**
+ * The width of the block in the cells of a column, in percent: between 40 and 80, and only a function
+ * of the index of the column among the caller's, so that nothing differs between the server and the
+ * client or between two renders, and the blocks do not line up.
+ */
+export function skeletonWidth(index: number): number {
+  return 40 + ((index * 17) % 41);
+}
+
+/**
+ * The rows of a grid that loads and has nothing to show yet: as many as the page holds. They are
+ * rows of Table's classes, so a variant stripes and rules them as it does the rows of data, and
+ * they are as tall as a row of data. They hold nothing and are hidden from what reads the page, and
+ * they are not rows of data: nothing in them is chosen or can have the keyboard.
+ */
+export function SkeletonRows() {
+  const { columns, skeletonRows } = useGridContext();
+  return Array.from({ length: skeletonRows }, (_, row) => {
+    let dataIndex = 0;
+    return (
+      <tr key={row} className="flg-table-row flg-data-grid-skeleton-row" aria-hidden="true">
+        {columns.map((column) => (
+          <td
+            key={column.id}
+            className="flg-table-cell flg-data-grid-skeleton-cell"
+            data-align={column.align}
+          >
+            {column.service ? null : (
+              <Skeleton shape="text" variant="pulse" width={`${skeletonWidth(dataIndex++)}%`} />
+            )}
+          </td>
+        ))}
+      </tr>
+    );
+  });
+}

## Sau khi thực thi

- Đẩy nhánh, rồi tạo ảnh chuẩn bằng workflow "Update visual baselines": 58 ảnh mới của 7 story giao diện (bốn của G1, ba ngoài mockup; mỗi story 4 chế độ × sáng, tối, cộng 2 ảnh `reduced-motion` của `GridLoading`). Xem ảnh trước khi xin review: `GridCore` khớp grid đầu tiên của g1 ở chế độ `normal` (Checkbox tiêu đề mixed, sắp hai cấp với số 1 và 2, dòng DH-1028 và DH-1025 đã chọn với nền và vạch 3px, dòng DH-1030 hover, khung focus trên ô Customer của DH-1026, khung cuộn tới dòng 4–11, thanh phân trang), với các khác biệt chờ sẵn của phát hiện 21 (header đặc, không cột ghim, không mục của thanh công cụ); `GridStriped`, `GridMinimal`, `GridCompact` giữ giao diện của Table; `GridLoading` (dòng skeleton cao bằng dòng), `GridReloading` (lớp phủ và Spinner dưới header), `GridEmpty` ("No data" ở giữa) như §4.3 tả; ảnh cũ của mọi component khác không đổi.
- Mô tả PR nêu cho chủ dự án những gì phát hiện 28 liệt kê, các quyết định Claude tự chốt và các mục để lại (phát hiện 29). Plan B không có changeset, nên merge PR này không mở PR "Version Packages"; `DataGrid` lên npm trong `0.5.0` (Plan G), và chủ dự án vẫn là người publish.

### Đã thực thi (2026-11-17)

- Bảy commit của nhánh nháp được cherry-pick lên `feat/phase-6-plan-b` (`6c813bd`, `db8a1f2`, `b2da9d9`, `77b699d`, `41592c7`, `2005196`, `373363d`). Cây giống hệt đầu nhánh nháp (`fdfb610`), cộng file plan.
- Mỗi task có một reviewer riêng (bảy reviewer chạy song song, chỉ đọc). Task 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7: Approved. Task 2: Needs fixes, vì `useRowKey` đọc trong lúc render một ref chỉ được ghi lúc commit (đổi `data` và hàm `rowKey` cùng lúc thì khoá cũ ở lại), và vì một grid mà mọi cột có độ rộng thì hẹp hơn khung `lined` của nó.
- Review toàn nhánh trên Opus, lấy góp ý của chủ dự án ở PR #41, #29 và #39 làm lăng kính: "With fixes" (5 Important, 12 Minor mới, cùng bảng phân loại 52 Minor của các review task). Bốn Important được chứng minh bằng probe fail trên `373363d`. Sửa trong một đợt, mỗi mục một commit (`67e3841`..`c7fc50d`):
  - **Hàm `rowKey` là hàm của lần render đó** (`67e3841`): bước làm phẳng nhận hàm của render; chỉ hàm đổi thì đọc lại khoá và giữ nguyên danh sách nếu mọi khoá như cũ; bỏ ref.
  - **Sau một lần nhấn bằng con trỏ, focus ở chỗ của ô hoạt động** (`7378703`, `c7fc50d`): nút sắp xếp huỷ `mousedown` và đưa focus về tiêu đề; Shift hay mod nhấn ở bất cứ đâu trên tiêu đề, Shift nhấn trên dòng hay ô chọn, và nhấn cạnh ô chọn cũng vậy; control mà một `cell` chứa giữ focus của nó (chế độ widget).
  - **Focus "ở trong" là ở trong DOM của bảng** (`6d9863c`): popup portal mà một ô mở không còn bị kéo focus về.
  - **Một hook giữ control của ô ngoài thứ tự Tab** (`82e3b22`, `use-release-controls.ts`): bỏ qua control trong popup của ô; `MutationObserver` trên `<tbody>` khi có cột `cell`, bắt control mà ô tự thêm.
  - **Không throw với prop sai dạng** (`03227d5`, `normalize.ts`), **mod+A theo `event.code`** (`46c8112`, `internal/letter-key.ts`, SearchField dùng chung), **một helper mỗi việc** (`3edeea1`), **`{...rest}` trước `data-variant`/`data-density`** (`b2e8b38`), **docs và spec đúng với code** (`17d68e4`).
  - **Cột đệm khi mọi cột có độ rộng** (`1049a3a`, `c7fc50d`): chủ dự án chọn phương án E trên trang so sánh ngày 2026-11-17. Bảng `width: Σpx` với `min-width: 100%` (không ngược lại: Firefox co khung về 0 trong một hộp theo nội dung); ô đệm `aria-hidden`, không nhận focus, phím bỏ qua, nhận hover của dòng, lần nhấn trên nó bị huỷ. Năm story `lined` không đổi một pixel (đo hộp ở ba engine); `GridStriped`, `GridMinimal` có ô đệm 2px (khung của chúng rộng hơn Σ 2px), sọc chạy tới mép như `striped` của Table.
  - Ngưỡng kích thước (`563b033`): JS (all exports) 63609 B, JS (DataGrid) 32169 B, CSS 19024 B.
  - Các dòng spec sửa, đánh dấu "(phát hiện khi review cuối Plan B)": §3.6, §3.7, §4.3, §5, §6.3.
  - Lần review lại: cả 11 mục đã xử lý; 3 Minor mới (cột đệm mất hover, Shift nhấn ngoài nút sắp xếp, dòng chú thích dài) sửa ở `c7fc50d`.
- **Quyết định Claude tự chốt khi thực thi** (chủ dự án có thể đảo lại):
  - Một `null` trong `selectedKeys` đã lưu thì cảnh báo; khoá không ứng với dòng nào thì bỏ qua lặng lẽ.
  - Hàm `rowKey` viết inline tốn một lượt đọc khoá mỗi lần render (hai ở development), không vẽ lại dòng khi khoá như cũ.
  - Ở `single`, vạch 3px của dòng đã chọn và khung focus của ô đầu gặp nhau thành cạnh trái 3px (Claude chụp sáng và tối).
